# Source: docs/openai.md

# OpenAI integration

`agent_weave_openai` uses `openai_dart 11.0.1` for typed provider transport.
AgentWeave implements orchestration and protocol adaptation around that SDK.

| Capability | Entry point |
| --- | --- |
| Responses chat | `OpenAIResponsesModel` |
| Chat Completions | `OpenAIChatModel` |
| Images | `OpenAIImageModel`, `imageTask`, or `client.images` |
| Speech | `OpenAISpeechModel`, `speechTask`, or `client.audio.speech` |
| Transcription | `OpenAITranscriptionModel`, `transcriptionTask`, or `client.audio.transcriptions` |
| Decisions | `OpenAIDecisionModel` or `client.decisions` |
| Embeddings | `OpenAIEmbeddingModel` or `client.embeddings` |
| Video jobs | `OpenAIVideoModel` or `client.videos` |
| Realtime | `OpenAIRealtimeModel`, `client.realtime`, or `client.realtimeSessions` |
| Supporting resources | Typed provider client resources |
| Additional JSON operations | `OpenAIPlatformApi` |

Use `configure` on chat adapters to set typed provider-specific options. Model
capabilities describe the adapter's request formats; selecting an incompatible
provider model can still produce a provider error.

The provider SDK also exposes conversations, files, uploads, batches, models,
moderation, fine-tuning, evals, containers, vector stores, skills, ChatKit,
webhooks, safety resources, Live sessions, saved agents, and Vaults. These are
delegated APIs, not independently implemented AgentWeave features.

`OpenAIPlatformApi` supports additional JSON requests and binary downloads,
including administration operations with an appropriate credential. It is an
explicit raw escape hatch. It does not imply typed or tested parity for every
OpenAI endpoint. Mutation requests through this helper are not automatically
retried.

The [operation inventory](openai-api-inventory.json) records the official
reference index for update reviews. Each entry is a discovery/review item, not
a passing endpoint test. See [validation](validation.md) for what was exercised.

## Media and realtime

`imageTask`, `speechTask`, and `transcriptionTask` emit normalized TanStack
generation results. Direct model wrappers retain provider-specific types.

Non-streaming image requests cannot abort in-flight through the underlying
SDK. Use its streaming operation when an abortable transport is required.
Cancelling a video wait does not cancel a provider job or its charges.
Close realtime connections explicitly when the session ends. The realtime
wrapper provides SDK connection access; AgentWeave does not yet orchestrate
voice turns, realtime tools, or device audio.

Use separate prefixed imports for realtime event classes:

```dart
import 'package:agent_weave_openai/agent_weave_openai.dart' as openai;
import 'package:agent_weave_openai/realtime.dart' as realtime;
```

The deprecated Assistants API has a separate `assistants.dart` import.
Provider/model deprecations remain OpenAI's schedule. In particular, the Speech
API models are scheduled to shut down on January 6, 2027; new voice integrations
should evaluate the Realtime API. Check the
[official speech guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/text-to-speech)
before choosing a model.

## Request-specific transport access

Use typed SDK resources first. For additional operations, `OpenAIPlatformApi`
provides `request` for JSON objects, `requestJson` for any JSON root, `send`
for response status/headers/bytes, and `download` for bytes. These methods accept
request-specific headers and repeated query values. Authentication and transport
headers remain client-owned. Mutations are not automatically retried.

```dart
final platform = openai.OpenAIPlatformApi(client);
final response = await platform.send(
  '/responses/your-response-id',
  repeatedQuery: {'include[]': ['reasoning.encrypted_content']},
  headers: {'Accept': 'application/json'},
);
print(response.headers['x-request-id']);
```

The raw helper buffers responses; it does not add arbitrary SSE or multipart
handling. It preserves data but does not implement missing tool/job lifecycles.


# Source: docs/openrouter.md

# Use OpenRouter

`agent_weave_openrouter` has a native JSON/SSE client and separate Chat and
Responses adapters. It reuses AgentWeave's compatible wire codecs, while native
routing, plugins, reasoning, cache options and metadata bypass the OpenAI SDK's
request serializer. This is selected integration, not complete OpenRouter parity.

Set `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `OPENROUTER_MODEL` in your backend environment for a
model available to your account. From the workspace root, run `dart pub get`,
then `dart run examples/openrouter_demo.dart`. This sends a real request and may
incur charges. The complete program is:

```dart
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:agent_weave/agent_weave.dart';
import 'package:agent_weave_openrouter/agent_weave_openrouter.dart' as router;

Future<void> main() async {
  final apiKey = Platform.environment['OPENROUTER_API_KEY'];
  final modelId = Platform.environment['OPENROUTER_MODEL'];
  if (apiKey == null || modelId == null) {
    throw StateError('Set OPENROUTER_API_KEY and OPENROUTER_MODEL.');
  }
  final client = router.OpenRouterClient.withApiKey(
    apiKey: apiKey,
    appName: 'My app',
    headers: {'X-OpenRouter-Metadata': 'enabled'},
  );
  try {
    final model = router.OpenRouterChatModel(
      client: client,
      model: modelId,
      options: router.OpenRouterChatOptions(
        provider: router.OpenRouterProviderPreferences(requireParameters: true),
      ),
    );
    final result = await generateText(model: model, prompt: 'Say hello.');
    print(result.text);
  } finally {
    client.close();
  }
}
```

The example was analyzed and compiled without execution. Keep credentials on the
backend. The caller closes the client at shutdown. An injected HTTP client or
`OpenRouterClient.withTransport` transport remains caller-owned. For rotating
secrets, use `OpenRouterClient(credentialResolver: yourTokenLoader)`; resolution
occurs per request within the request deadline. Attribution and session headers
are configured on the client; authorization belongs to the resolver.

## Native options

`OpenRouterChatOptions` and `OpenRouterResponsesOptions` keep native fields
separate from runtime-owned messages, tools, schema, token bounds and streaming.
They take immutable snapshots, including nested `extra` values. OpenRouter
reports usage automatically; deprecated usage-inclusion flags do not control it.

```dart
final options = router.OpenRouterChatOptions(
  provider: router.OpenRouterProviderPreferences(
    order: ['provider-selected-by-your-app'],
    allowFallbacks: false,
    requireParameters: true,
    dataCollection: router.OpenRouterDataCollection.deny,
    sort: router.OpenRouterProviderSort.price,
    maxPrice: {'prompt': '1', 'completion': '2'},
  ),
  reasoning: router.OpenRouterReasoning(
    effort: router.OpenRouterReasoningEffort.low,
  ),
  cacheControl: router.OpenRouterCacheControl(),
  plugins: [router.OpenRouterPlugin(id: 'response-healing')],
  extra: {'prompt_cache_key': 'application-scoped-key'},
);
```

This is configuration syntax, not a tested provider/model combination. Provider
availability, supported parameters, plugin behavior and price units follow the
[official routing contract](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/routing/provider-selection).
Do not assume every combination works. `requireParameters` asks OpenRouter to
filter providers that cannot support the requested parameters.

Provider preferences also expose allow/ignore lists, ZDR, quantizations,
distillable-text enforcement, provider-specific options and performance
preferences. Nested price, percentile and provider-option structures remain
JSON so their schema unions and unknown fields survive. `extra` supports newer
native options. A recognized field is not proof of orchestration or acceptance.

The optional `configure` callback remains SDK-typed for compatible request
parameters. Prefer `request.copyWith(...)`; rebuilding a request through the
SDK's typed JSON input decoder can reject raw reasoning items. Native fields
belong in `options` or `extra`. Neither path can replace runtime history or
registered function definitions. Native JSON client methods are separate for
requests the normalized agent does not implement.

## Responses and private replay

Use `OpenRouterResponsesModel(client: client, model: modelId, options: ...)`
for `/responses`. It has its own private replay namespace. OpenRouter Responses
is stateless: send complete input history. The adapter rejects `store: true` and
non-null `previous_response_id`; it does not depend on a server-stored response.
It excludes automatic OpenAI encrypted-reasoning includes; OpenRouter documents
automatic encrypted content for supported reasoning providers.

Returned Responses output items retain opaque fields and order through the next
tool turn. Chat retains ordered `reasoning_details` fragments as returned, in
`openrouter.chat.reasoning`, and replays them only to the Chat endpoint. It does
not sort or deduplicate blocks. If only plaintext `reasoning` is returned, it
streams as reasoning text and is privately retained in
`openrouter.chat.reasoning_text` for the next turn. Structured details take
precedence when both representations are returned. The fixture verifies ordered replay, not every
provider's incremental-fragment behavior. Unknown or cross-provider private
history is not substituted for this provider's replay. File handles owned by
another provider are rejected; Responses URL and inline document sources remain
separate from provider-owned IDs. Chat document parts are not implemented.

## Metadata and native responses

`X-OpenRouter-Metadata: enabled` opts into router metadata when supplied by the
service. The adapter retains actual generation/model/provider identity, usage,
cost and unknown response metadata in private assistant `providerData` under
`openrouter.chat.metadata` or `openrouter.responses.metadata`. Missing values
stay absent. It does not infer the provider or compute an invoice. Reasoning and
metadata stay out of UI hydration; `AgentResult` is trusted backend data.

Normalized metadata is a compact merged snapshot. It is not a log of every
stream frame. For complete native envelopes, headers and event IDs, use
`client.createChat`, `streamChat`, `createResponse`, or `streamResponse`. Native
JSON responses expose `data`, `statusCode` and headers. Streaming preserves
unknown event fields and detects inline errors and premature EOF.

The native client does not implement management APIs or every modality. Hosted
server tools, background-job handling, output media and all model variants still
need dedicated runtime behavior. See the [API inventory](openrouter-api-reference.md)
for all pinned operations and fields, including those not integrated.

## Errors and cancellation

Direct streams propagate redacted `JsonHttpException` diagnostics.
`generateText` wraps failures in `AgentRunException`; use its `code`, and inspect
`cause` only on the trusted backend. Error details and headers may contain private
provider information, so do not send them to a UI. Resolver failures and malformed
stream payloads use generic messages. Known request credentials are redacted.

Requests have per-call deadlines and cancellation. Cancelling one subscription
signals that call without cancelling siblings sharing a parent token; cancelling
the parent signals all active calls. This does not undo requests already accepted
remotely. The client does not automatically retry POSTs.

## Validation and migration

Offline loopback cases exercise Chat and Responses schema output, persisted tool
approval and replay, opaque reasoning, metadata, error privacy, rotating
credentials, cancellation and client ownership. They do not establish live model
support, cache hits, routing, billing, or all native fields.

Earlier development versions returned an `OpenAIClient` from `openRouterClient`
and exported SDK routing types. `openRouterClient` now returns `OpenRouterClient`.
Use `options: OpenRouterChatOptions(...)` for provider/reasoning/fallback settings;
use native enums and non-const option constructors for immutable snapshots.
Consumers explicitly typing the old SDK client must migrate. `configure` remains
available for SDK-compatible parameters. See [coverage](provider-coverage.md),
[validation](validation.md) and [the independent review](dx-review.md).


# Source: docs/openrouter-api-reference.md

# OpenRouter API inventory

Source: [OpenRouter OpenAPI](https://openrouter.ai/openapi.json), reviewed 2026-11-04, SHA-256 `07b8b1ac91ba9e522540417420cd74004db5246d5341e5c86d68443e4438af82`. The source declares the MIT license.

The pinned schema describes 146 operations across 108 paths. Chat completions and Responses have selected integrations; all other operations are inventoried and not integrated.

The [machine-readable inventory](openrouter-api-inventory.json) records each operation, request, response, parameter and header contract, and each component field, union and constraint. Credential-shaped example values are redacted. Original-source and sanitized-snapshot hashes are separate. References point to the schema snapshot in `tool/contracts/openrouter/openapi.json`. A schema entry or native field forwarding does not establish supported runtime orchestration or model behavior.

Run `python3 tool/openrouter_contract.py --check` offline to verify the snapshot and generated outputs. `--upstream` compares the current official document without updating any files. See `tool/contracts/openrouter/README.md` for attribution and source provenance.

# Source: docs/together.md

# Use Together Chat Completions

`agent_weave_together` provides a native Together Chat Completions client and a
`ChatModel` adapter. The agent runtime owns tool execution, approvals, and
history. Model support for tools, schemas, images, video, and audio varies.

## Run a backend request

From the workspace root, run `dart pub get`. Save this example as
`examples/together_demo.dart`. Set `TOGETHER_API_KEY` and `TOGETHER_MODEL` in
your backend environment, choosing a model available to your account. Running
the example makes a paid provider request. Keep the key on the backend.

```dart
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:agent_weave/agent_weave.dart';
import 'package:agent_weave_together/agent_weave_together.dart' as together;

Future<void> main() async {
  final key = Platform.environment['TOGETHER_API_KEY'];
  final modelId = Platform.environment['TOGETHER_MODEL'];
  if (key == null || modelId == null) {
    throw StateError('Set TOGETHER_API_KEY and TOGETHER_MODEL.');
  }
  final client = together.TogetherClient(apiKey: key);
  try {
    final model = together.TogetherChatModel(
      client: client,
      model: modelId,
      options: together.TogetherChatOptions(temperature: 0.3),
    );
    final result = await generateText(model: model, prompt: 'Say hello.');
    print(result.text);
  } finally {
    client.close();
  }
}
```

Run `dart run examples/together_demo.dart` to print the response. The same
model works with `AiAgent` and its registered tools, approvals, schema output,
and history. See [tools and approvals](tools.md) and the
[Dart API guide](dart-api.md).

## Choose typed options or native JSON

See [all reviewed request fields](together-options.md) for their Dart entry points.

`TogetherChatOptions` snapshots its input values and exposes typed options,
including enums for compliance, context length behavior, and reasoning effort.
`logprobs` is an integer from 0 to 20. The runtime owns `max_tokens` through
`ModelRequest.maxOutputTokens` or the corresponding agent setting. The agent
adapter requests one choice (`n: 1`).

For multiple choices (`n > 1`), legacy `function_call`, or other native fields,
use `TogetherClient.createChat` or `streamChat` with native JSON. These methods
return native JSON; `streamChat` sets `stream: true`. The agent adapter does not
normalize legacy function calls. Native JSON access does not establish support
for every Together operation.

The agent adapter rejects document inputs. Inline audio must be WAV. Image,
video, audio, tool, and schema acceptance depends on the selected model.

## Handle requests and errors

The default request timeout is two minutes for the entire HTTP request. Set
`requestTimeout` on `TogetherClient` to change it. Timeout and a user-provided
`CancellationToken` abort the HTTP request. Cancelling a native stream
subscription also aborts that request without closing the shared client. The client does not automatically
retry POST requests. Close the `TogetherClient` when finished. If you inject an
HTTP client, you own and must close that HTTP client.

A `TogetherException` provides `statusCode`, `requestId`, and optional JSON
`details` to trusted backend code. Its `toString()` omits provider response
bodies. Do not expose a provider error's cause or details to the UI; they can
contain private data. Protect logs and avoid logging request or response bodies.

A `length` finish returns partial text with `finishReason: 'length'`. Truncated
tool calls fail rather than execute. Choose output limits appropriate to your
application and handle partial results.

## Review the pinned contract

The AST-generated [chat inventory](together-chat-inventory.json) records 27
top-level request fields and their dispositions for the pinned declaration. It
is an inventory, not a certification of nested fields, response handling,
lifecycle, models, or other operations. The pin is in
`tool/contracts/together/source.json`; dispositions are in
`tool/contracts/together/coverage.json`. Headers and query parameters are
captured as maps; this does not claim coverage of every operation.

From the repository root, install the inventory tool dependencies and run the
checks:

```sh
npm ci --prefix tool/interop --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
dart run tool/together_contract.dart
node tool/interop/inventory.mjs --check
```

`node tool/interop/inventory.mjs --upstream` compares the pinned files with
upstream main. Review changes before running `--write` to update the inventory.
Offline fixtures cover selected requests and streams. No live Together request,
model acceptance, or billing has been verified.

The normal checks include an independent, runnable offline consumer:

```sh
dart --enable-asserts run examples/review_cases/together.dart
```

It exercises a real loopback HTTP service, schema output, tool approval and
continuation, private reasoning replay, partial output and backend diagnostics.
Response log probabilities, prompt echoes, warnings and arbitrary provider
metadata are available through the raw native client and are not normalized into
`AgentResult`. Message names and URL audio also require native requests.


# Source: docs/cloudflare.md

# Cloudflare Workers AI and AI Gateway

`agent_weave_cloudflare` provides REST clients and selected model adapters. The
contracts below are distinct; a model's support for one does not establish its
support for another. Model availability, options, pricing, gateway behavior and
live inference have not been verified by the offline fixtures.

| Contract | Client | Request |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Workers AI native | `CloudflareClient` | `POST /accounts/{accountId}/ai/run/{model}` with model-specific input |
| Gateway run | `CloudflareGatewayClient` | `POST /accounts/{accountId}/ai/run` wrapping `model`, `input`, and optional `options` |
| Compatible Chat | `CloudflareCompatibleClient` | `/accounts/{accountId}/ai/v1/chat/completions` |
| Compatible Responses | `CloudflareCompatibleClient` | `/accounts/{accountId}/ai/v1/responses` |

The native client also exposes `getModelSchema`, `listModels`, raw JSON, bytes,
and SSE methods. Raw methods preserve status, headers, bytes and, when present,
JSON; they do not validate every model's schema. Gateway options can be passed
to the gateway and compatible clients. `@cf/` models require a gateway ID for
the gateway run contract. The compatible endpoints have separate payloads and
stream semantics; select the adapter supported by the chosen model.

## Start a backend chat

Set `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`, `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and
`CLOUDFLARE_CHAT_MODEL` for a model available to your account. For Workers AI
models routed through Gateway, also set `CLOUDFLARE_GATEWAY_ID`.
The API token needs Account > Workers AI > Read permission, including when
calling third-party models. AI Gateway management permission alone is insufficient.

The complete `examples/cloudflare_demo.dart` program is:

```dart
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:agent_weave/agent_weave.dart';
import 'package:agent_weave_cloudflare/agent_weave_cloudflare.dart' as cf;

Future<void> main() async {
  final accountId = Platform.environment['CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID'];
  final apiToken = Platform.environment['CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN'];
  final modelId = Platform.environment['CLOUDFLARE_CHAT_MODEL'];
  final gatewayId = Platform.environment['CLOUDFLARE_GATEWAY_ID'];
  if (accountId == null || apiToken == null || modelId == null) {
    throw StateError(
      'Set CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID, CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN and CLOUDFLARE_CHAT_MODEL.',
    );
  }
  if (modelId.startsWith('@cf/') && gatewayId == null) {
    throw StateError(
      'Set CLOUDFLARE_GATEWAY_ID for Workers AI gateway requests.',
    );
  }
  final workers = cf.CloudflareClient.withApiToken(
    accountId: accountId,
    apiToken: apiToken,
    gateway: gatewayId == null
        ? null
        : cf.CloudflareGatewayOptions(gatewayId: gatewayId),
  );
  try {
    final model = cf.CloudflareCompatibleChatModel(
      client: cf.CloudflareCompatibleClient(client: workers),
      model: modelId,
    );
    final result = await generateText(model: model, prompt: 'Say hello.');
    print(result.text);
  } finally {
    workers.close();
  }
}
```

Run `dart run examples/cloudflare_demo.dart` from the workspace. It sends a real
inference request and may incur charges. This example was analyzed and compiled,
but not run against Cloudflare. Keep credentials on the backend.

For rotating secrets, construct `CloudflareClient` with an application-owned
`tokenResolver`. It runs per request within that request's timeout. Requests
use Bearer authorization. The optional client `gateway` supplies default
Gateway headers to native inference and compatible endpoints; explicit
request-level Gateway options override matching defaults. A model-in-path
request can therefore carry the gateway ID needed for prepaid Gateway billing.
Actual billing behavior has not been tested.

Gateway options include cache key, TTL, bypass, metadata, timeout and retry
headers. A cache key can group responses: choose it with the application's data
isolation and privacy requirements in mind. Custom Gateway headers cannot
override authentication or built-in option headers. The client does not retry
POSTs itself; Gateway retry headers request gateway-side behavior.

With an application-owned `workers` client, native inference is separate from
the compatible Chat adapter:

```dart
final embeddings = await cf.CloudflareEmbeddingModel(client: workers).embed(
  cf.CloudflareEmbeddingRequest(text: ['hello'], pooling: cf.CloudflarePooling.cls),
);
print(embeddings.vectors);
print(embeddings.pooling); // Actual returned pooling, never an inferred default.

final gateway = cf.CloudflareGatewayClient(client: workers);
final response = await gateway.runJson(
  modelId,
  {'messages': [{'role': 'user', 'content': 'Hello'}]},
  gateway: cf.CloudflareGatewayOptions(gatewayId: gatewayId),
);
print(response.json);
```

## Model adapters

- `CloudflareEmbeddingModel` supports the BGE `text` input and optional
  `CloudflarePooling.mean` or `.cls`. Its result exposes `vectors`, `shape`,
  returned `pooling`, `result`, and the full `response`.
- `CloudflareTranscriptionModel` accepts `CloudflareAudioInput.json` for
  model-specific JSON or `.bytes` for binary input, with a configurable content
  type defaulting to `application/octet-stream`. The exact binary REST content
  type and server acceptance have not been live verified. The result exposes
  text and raw result data.
- `CloudflareImageModel` accepts model-specific JSON. It returns image bytes for
  image content types and decodes the base64 `result.image` for Flux Schnell;
  retain `response` for raw JSON and metadata. Unknown formats require raw
  client inspection. Image format and model acceptance remain model-specific.

For an agent, prefer `CloudflareCompatibleChatModel` with an explicitly chosen,
currently available compatible model, configured by the application (for
example via an environment variable). `CloudflareCompatibleResponsesModel`
uses the separate Responses contract. Both expose `options` and an SDK-typed
`configure` callback; request-owned fields cannot be overridden through
`options`. Compatible Chat defaults to `max_completion_tokens`; select
`CloudflareChatTokenField.maxTokens` for models requiring `max_tokens`.

For example, configure the compatible Chat adapter with a model supplied by the
application:

```dart
final compatible = cf.CloudflareCompatibleClient(client: workers);
final chat = cf.CloudflareCompatibleChatModel(
  client: compatible,
  model: compatibleModelFromEnvironment,
);
```

`CloudflareChatModel` requires an explicit model and implements the documented
Hermes traditional single-tool continuation. It performs non-streamed native
requests even when used through the core stream API, accepts text parts, and
rejects multi-call continuation. Its structured-output mode sends a bare JSON
schema. Availability of the legacy Hermes model has not been verified; do not
assume that another native model supports this continuation format. Tool
execution and approvals remain the runtime's responsibility.

## Lifecycle and evidence

Pass a `CancellationToken` to client methods and model operations as needed.
Request timeouts include preparation; cancellation cannot undo an operation
already accepted remotely. Close the client when done. An injected transport
or HTTP client remains caller-owned. Cancelling one subscription signals that invocation without cancelling sibling
calls sharing its parent token. Cancelling the parent signals all active calls.
Streaming subscription cancellation aborts the request when supported by the
underlying HTTP client. No license acceptance
or paid inference occurs automatically.

Offline fixtures exercise selected request and response behavior, not live model
availability, full API parity, provider billing, or server acceptance. Consult
[Workers AI REST](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/get-started/rest-api/),
[function calling](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/features/function-calling/),
[JSON mode](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/features/json-mode/), and
[AI Gateway REST](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/usage/rest-api/)
for current provider requirements. See [provider coverage](provider-coverage.md)
and [compatibility](compatibility.md) for the scope of this integration. The
[API inventory reference](cloudflare-api-reference.md) records the classified
contracts; it is not a parity certificate. The inventory includes management
endpoints that are not integrated. Compatible endpoint documentation is tracked
separately from the pinned API specification.


# Source: docs/cloudflare-api-reference.md

# Cloudflare API inventory

Source: [Cloudflare OpenAPI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cloudflare/api-schemas/193e683baba9c46b675d91c959c3b9a726b2d184/openapi.json), revision `193e683baba9c46b675d91c959c3b9a726b2d184`, reviewed 2026-11-04.

The pinned schema contains 82 operations across 50 Workers AI and AI Gateway paths. Four operations have selected AgentWeave integrations. The rest remain explicitly unimplemented.

Download the [machine-readable inventory](cloudflare-api-inventory.json) for nested request and response fields, unions, required flags, defaults, enum values and parameter constraints. These are specification entries, not claims that AgentWeave executes every option.

Model documentation schemas are attributed to Cloudflare under CC BY 4.0, with unmodified snapshots and generated field inventories. The OpenAPI source is BSD-3-Clause. See the retained licenses and attribution in `tool/contracts/cloudflare/README.md`.

The complete selected source schemas and BSD license are retained in `tool/contracts/cloudflare/`. Run `python3 tool/cloudflare_contract.py --check` offline. Refresh with `--extract /path/to/official/openapi.json` only after reviewing the revision and upstream changes. New operations receive `not-integrated` status automatically.

See [Cloudflare usage](cloudflare.md) for auth, native model inputs, compatible protocols, cancellation and known limits.

## Selected public model schemas

The inventory retains the full input/output JSON schema for BGE base English, Whisper and Flux Schnell. Public documentation URLs are unversioned. Each downloaded snapshot has a SHA-256 hash; they are not attributed to the OpenAPI Git revision.

| Snapshot | Official source | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bge-input.json` | [Schema](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/models/bge-base-en-v1.5/sync-input.json) | `0291aab34abe8e4657ead038aba73f37098ab8f94888e7d99e4791a4adfcb353` |
| `bge-output.json` | [Schema](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/models/bge-base-en-v1.5/sync-output.json) | `4f25a95d82f8b25fb9f386fc35b1ee244fa7437a7fc75db7506aa66daa6d9541` |
| `whisper-input.json` | [Schema](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/models/whisper/schema-input.json) | `e82ea39d3b7aef1058accc4e5a5c27c5817b30f16cd9c04a6cb6eded41edb944` |
| `whisper-output.json` | [Schema](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/models/whisper/schema-output.json) | `d6f939cc1591e5f6176e1e0a7d64ac8b976d0c55d9fdba9b435d260c1710a2da` |
| `flux-input.json` | [Schema](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/models/flux-1-schnell/schema-input.json) | `d17b781a278e8f00233de3c93b1ac73ed07ba609204674338749c1df38c16b17` |
| `flux-output.json` | [Schema](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/models/flux-1-schnell/schema-output.json) | `5528a6a3b29dec4480fd67a9d695300ad5616c54372afb51988ee660c87a32c6` |

Whisper declares a binary-string input variant, but this schema does not establish an accepted REST Content-Type. The typed binary path has serialization tests only. Native `/run` model schemas vary; forwarding raw fields does not certify those models.

Model schemas, Gateway request headers, Workers bindings, asynchronous batch APIs and compatible endpoints require separate reviews when the OpenAPI omits them. No live Cloudflare calls were made for this inventory.


# Source: docs/vercel-gateway.md

# Use Vercel AI Gateway

`agent_weave_vercel_gateway` provides `GatewayChatModel` for the public Chat
Completions endpoint and `GatewayResponsesModel` for the public Responses
endpoint. They use different request and stream formats. Neither uses the
internal Vercel AI SDK V4 language-model wire protocol.

## Send a request

From the workspace root, run `dart pub get`. Save the following as
`examples/gateway_demo.dart`. Set `GATEWAY_API_KEY`, `GATEWAY_MODEL`, and
`GATEWAY_PROVIDER` in your backend environment. Choose a model and a provider
available to your account. Running the example makes a paid request.

```dart
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:agent_weave/agent_weave.dart';
import 'package:agent_weave_vercel_gateway/agent_weave_vercel_gateway.dart' as gateway;

Future<void> main() async {
  final key = Platform.environment['GATEWAY_API_KEY'];
  final modelId = Platform.environment['GATEWAY_MODEL'];
  final provider = Platform.environment['GATEWAY_PROVIDER'];
  if (key == null || modelId == null || provider == null) {
    throw StateError('Set GATEWAY_API_KEY, GATEWAY_MODEL, and GATEWAY_PROVIDER.');
  }
  final client = gateway.GatewayClient.withApiKey(apiKey: key);
  try {
    final model = gateway.GatewayChatModel(
      client: client,
      model: modelId,
      options: gateway.GatewayOptions(order: [provider]),
    );
    final result = await generateText(model: model, prompt: 'Say hello.');
    print(result.text);
  } finally {
    client.close();
  }
}
```

Run `dart run examples/gateway_demo.dart`. The response prints to the terminal.
To use Responses, replace `GatewayChatModel` with `GatewayResponsesModel`.
The same models work with `AiAgent` and its tools, approvals, and stored
history. See the [Dart API guide](dart-api.md).

## Resolve credentials per request

For a rotating Gateway token or bring-your-own-key (BYOK) credentials, use a
resolver. This example reads the environment each time the client makes a
request. Save it as `examples/gateway_byok_demo.dart`, and set
`GATEWAY_API_KEY`, `GATEWAY_MODEL`, and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` on the backend.
Choose a model available through the Anthropic provider. Running the example
makes a paid request.

```dart
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:agent_weave/agent_weave.dart';
import 'package:agent_weave_vercel_gateway/agent_weave_vercel_gateway.dart' as gateway;

String requiredEnvironment(String name) {
  final value = Platform.environment[name];
  if (value == null || value.isEmpty) throw StateError('Set $name.');
  return value;
}

Future<void> main() async {
  final modelId = requiredEnvironment('GATEWAY_MODEL');
  final client = gateway.GatewayClient(
    credentialResolver: () => gateway.GatewayCredentials(
      token: requiredEnvironment('GATEWAY_API_KEY'),
      byok: {
        'anthropic': [
          {'apiKey': requiredEnvironment('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY')},
        ],
      },
    ),
  );
  try {
    final model = gateway.GatewayResponsesModel(client: client, model: modelId);
    final result = await generateText(model: model, prompt: 'Say hello.');
    print(result.text);
  } finally {
    client.close();
  }
}
```

Replace the environment reads with your backend secret manager to rotate
credentials while the process runs. BYOK credential fields differ by provider.
Credentials belong in `GatewayCredentials`, not `GatewayOptions` or ordinary
`providerOptions`.

## Options and raw responses

`GatewayOptions` serializes routing preferences such as `models`, `order`, and
`only`, plus cache, timeout, privacy, and other fields. Both models also accept
provider-specific JSON through `providerOptions`. Serialization fixtures do not
prove that the live Gateway or a selected provider accepts or honors each field,
nor do they establish cost or billing behavior.

For native JSON, use `GatewayClient.createChat`, `streamChat`, `createResponse`,
or `streamResponse`. Nonstreaming results include native JSON, status, and
headers. Streams expose event envelopes and retain unknown metadata. Model
adapters normalize a limited set of fields; they do not invent a selected
provider identity from unverified metadata.

Responses accepts document URLs and inline data, but the high-level Gateway
adapter blocks file IDs. Chat does not accept documents or audio output. Model
and provider input support varies. See [documents](documents.md).

## Request lifetime and privacy

Credential resolution runs inside each request's deadline. The default total
deadline is two minutes; configure `requestTimeout` on `GatewayClient` or its
transport. A cancellation token or expired deadline prevents a late credential
resolver from dispatching the request. Close the Gateway client at shutdown.
`GatewayClient.withTransport` borrows its transport, and an injected HTTP client
is also caller-owned. Close borrowed resources yourself.

Errors are redacted using the request's credentials. Treat raw error details and
backend logs as private, and never send credentials or provider error details to
clients. AgentWeave stores model content in history, not request credentials.
A provider could still echo a secret in its model output, so the application
must protect any content it sends or stores.

Offline fixtures cover selected request and stream behavior, including Chat
continuation. Live Gateway behavior, provider selection, model acceptance, and
billing have not been verified. See [provider coverage](provider-coverage.md).

## Track option updates

The generated [option reference](gateway-options.md) maps 16 named options from
the pinned official SDK to their Dart entry points. It distinguishes typed
routing, request credentials, native extensions and SDK-only features. This is
an update-review aid, not proof of public endpoint or model behavior.

Use `GatewayCaching`, `GatewayServiceTier`, and `GatewayProviderSort` for fixed
option values. Unrepresented service-owned fields can use `GatewayOptions.extra`;
it rejects credentials, typed-field replacement and client-only image decoding.
Conditional Decisions fallbacks, batch jobs and image decoding are not implemented
by these Chat/Responses adapters.

After `npm ci --prefix tool/interop --ignore-scripts`, reproduce the field check:

```sh
dart run tool/gateway_contract.dart
node tool/interop/gateway-inventory.mjs --check
```

The independent consumer exercise is also runnable without a provider key:

```sh
dart --enable-asserts run examples/review_cases/gateway.dart
```

# Gateway option reference

Generated from Vercel's SDK commit `6adf8c797d5e2bf056c077f946aa12dabb3cb268`. This is an
option inventory, not a certificate of public endpoint behavior. Read the
[Gateway guide](vercel-gateway.md) for setup and limits.

| Wire option | Dart entry point | Disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| byok | GatewayCredentials.byok via credentialResolver | request-credentials |
| caching | GatewayOptions.caching | typed-option |
| experimental_streamingImageDecoding | Not sent; image decoding is outside Chat/Responses | sdk-client-only |
| disallowPromptTraining | GatewayOptions.disallowPromptTraining | typed-option |
| has | GatewayOptions.has | typed-option |
| idempotencyKey | GatewayOptions.extra; no batch lifecycle implementation | native-extension |
| models | GatewayOptions.models; string fallbacks only | typed-option |
| only | GatewayOptions.only | typed-option |
| order | GatewayOptions.order | typed-option |
| providerTimeouts | GatewayOptions.byokProviderTimeouts | typed-option |
| quotaEntityId | GatewayOptions.quotaEntityId | typed-option |
| serviceTier | GatewayOptions.serviceTier | typed-option |
| sort | GatewayOptions.sort | typed-option |
| tags | GatewayOptions.tags | typed-option |
| user | GatewayOptions.user | typed-option |
| zeroDataRetention | GatewayOptions.zeroDataRetention | typed-option |

The public Chat and Responses extension uses `providerOptions.gateway`.
BYOK credentials are resolved per request and are excluded from ordinary option
serialization. Unknown service-owned options can use `GatewayOptions.extra`;
that does not prove their endpoint applicability. Conditional decision fallbacks
and the SDK's image decoder are outside these adapters.

See the [machine-readable inventory](gateway-options-inventory.json). Do not
edit this generated page by hand; review the pin and run
`node tool/interop/gateway-inventory.mjs --write`.

# Source: docs/anthropic.md

# Anthropic Messages

Use `AnthropicNativeClient` for native JSON and SSE access, including fields the
pinned Dart SDK does not know. Its `chatModel` also integrates supported
Messages streams with AgentWeave's text, structured output and tool loop. The
package is independent and unofficial.

## Run the example

From the workspace, set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` in the
backend environment, then run `dart run examples/anthropic_demo.dart`. Optionally
set `ANTHROPIC_VERSION`; it defaults to `2023-06-01` for backwards
compatibility. The example requests adaptive thinking, caching and structured
output, so choose a model and API version that support that combination. It
makes a billable request. See [Anthropic's versioning documentation](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/api/versioning)
and verify the current model and feature requirements before selecting a newer
version.

The example's `configure` receives a read-only JSON snapshot. Return a new map,
as it does with `...body`. The agent owns messages, max tokens, system
instructions and tools, and protects the runtime output schema. You can add
supported native options without replacing these values; this does not imply
AgentWeave implements the behavior of every forwarded field.

```dart
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:agent_weave/agent_weave.dart';
import 'package:agent_weave_anthropic/agent_weave_anthropic.dart' as anthropic;

Future<void> main() async {
  final apiKey = Platform.environment['ANTHROPIC_API_KEY'];
  final modelId = Platform.environment['ANTHROPIC_MODEL'];
  if (apiKey == null || apiKey.isEmpty || modelId == null || modelId.isEmpty) {
    throw StateError('Set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_MODEL.');
  }
  final client = anthropic.AnthropicNativeClient.withApiKey(
    apiKey: apiKey,
    apiVersion: Platform.environment['ANTHROPIC_VERSION'] ?? '2023-06-01',
  );
  try {
    final model = client.chatModel(
      model: modelId,
      configure: (body) => {
        ...body,
        'thinking': {'type': 'adaptive'},
        'cache_control': {'type': 'ephemeral'},
      },
    );
    final result = await generateObject<String>(
      model: model,
      prompt: 'Give one concise title for a guide to growing herbs indoors.',
      schema: const {
        'type': 'object',
        'properties': {
          'title': {'type': 'string'},
        },
        'required': ['title'],
        'additionalProperties': false,
      },
      decode: (json) => (json as Map<String, Object?>)['title'] as String,
    );
    print(result.value);
  } finally {
    client.close();
  }
}
```

## Native requests and streams

`client.createMessage(body)` returns an `AnthropicNativeResponse` with the raw
JSON in `data`, HTTP `statusCode`, and sanitized response `headers`.
`client.countTokens(body)` calls the native token-counting endpoint and returns
the same response shape, including fields such as `input_tokens` when supplied
by the service. Both methods and `streamMessages(body)` accept per-request
`headers`, `query` and `cancellation`; query values are lists of strings.
`streamMessages` yields `JsonSseData` with raw event `data`, event name, ID and
response headers. Error details retain private provider content after credential
scrubbing; do not expose them directly in a UI or logs. It requires a complete stream ending in `message_stop`.
`send` provides native JSON access to other paths without claiming endpoint
coverage.

The client defaults to API version `2023-06-01`; set `apiVersion` explicitly
when your integration needs another version. Constructor options `betas`,
`workspaceId`, and `userProfileId` set headers. In particular the
`anthropic-workspace-id` and `anthropic-user-profile-id` headers are separate
from any `workspace_id` and `user_profile_id` fields you put in a native JSON
body. Check the provider contract for the endpoint and version you use.

A `credentialResolver` can fetch or rotate a key for each request; alternatively
use `withApiKey`. Keep credentials on the backend. Close the native client when
finished; an injected `http.Client` is borrowed and remains the caller's
responsibility. There are no automatic retries. Cancellation aborts local
request work; it does not undo a request or external effect already accepted by
the provider.

## SDK-backed facade

Existing integrations can still construct `AnthropicChatModel` with an
`anthropic_sdk_dart` `AnthropicClient` and a typed `MessageCreateRequest`
`configure` callback. The SDK client is caller-owned. The typed callback's patch
preserves unknown unchanged JSON fields; edits to fields or lists can replace the
corresponding values. The SDK's typed representation still cannot express every
new provider field. Prefer the native client for unknown fields and
request-scoped transport cancellation.

## Replay and limits

The agent preserves provider content blocks for continuation, including
signatures and unknown fields on supported block types. This replay data and raw
responses may contain sensitive content; keep them private on the backend and
out of user-facing hydration or logs. The normalized agent currently handles
text, thinking, redacted thinking, client tool-use and pinned hosted-tool blocks with supported
text, thinking, signature and input JSON deltas. Citation deltas are retained
privately on text blocks for replay; there is no normalized UI citation event. Unknown block types or deltas
fail explicitly. Hosted tools and bounded `pause_turn` continuation are integrated; see the
[hosted-tool guide](anthropic-hosted.md). Audio/video, MCP, browser tools and
complete nested semantics remain unfinished. Use raw native access for other
protocols.
For client computer use, see the [computer-use guide](anthropic-computer.md).
File-ID document parts are supported by the native agent path; the typed SDK
configuration path cannot yet decode them. URL and supported inline documents
are also available.

See the [request field inventory](anthropic-parameters.md) for the pinned
contract and disposition of each field. Fixtures exercise selected behavior;
they do not establish live model support or complete endpoint parity.

## Upstream SDK cancellation fix

[SDK PR #432](https://github.com/davidmigloz/ai_clients_dart/pull/432) adds prompt
cancellation before response headers, during stalled bodies, and through the
public stream wrappers while retaining shared-client ownership. The contribution
is submitted, not merged or released. AgentWeave's native client already uses
its own shared transport and does not require this unreleased SDK change.


# Source: docs/anthropic-hosted.md

# Anthropic hosted tools

Add provider-executed search, fetch, code execution or tool search to an ordinary
AgentWeave agent. Your `Tool` registrations remain application-executed; hosted
tools do not call their executors or produce local approval requests.

This complete example makes a billable request when you run it. Choose a model
that accepts web search and set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`.

```dart
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:agent_weave/agent_weave.dart';
import 'package:agent_weave_anthropic/agent_weave_anthropic.dart' as anthropic;

Future<void> main() async {
  final key = Platform.environment['ANTHROPIC_API_KEY'];
  final modelId = Platform.environment['ANTHROPIC_MODEL'];
  if (key == null || key.isEmpty || modelId == null || modelId.isEmpty) {
    throw StateError('Set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_MODEL.');
  }
  final client = anthropic.AnthropicNativeClient.withApiKey(apiKey: key);
  try {
    final agent = AiAgent<void>(
      model: client.chatModel(
        model: modelId,
        hostedTools: [
          anthropic.AnthropicHostedTool(
            const anthropic.WebSearchTool(maxUses: 3),
          ),
        ],
      ),
      maxSteps: 4,
      maxOutputTokens: 1024,
    );
    final result = await agent.generate(
      ChatRequest(
        threadId: 'research',
        runId: 'first',
        messages: [
          ChatMessage.user(
            'Find the latest stable Dart release.',
            id: 'question',
          ),
        ],
      ),
      ownerId: 'local-example',
      context: null,
    );
    print(result.text);
  } finally {
    client.close();
  }
}
```

## Configure hosted tools

`AnthropicHostedTool` snapshots a typed SDK `BuiltInTool`. Its `fromJson`
constructor retains unknown native option fields. Both constructors check an
explicit supported type/name pair and exclude client-executed tools such as
bash, memory, browser and computer. They also reject conflicting domain lists.
Other nested options and model acceptance are validated by the provider.

The current source pin contains 15 type spellings across web search, web fetch,
code execution and regex/BM25 tool search, including the unversioned tool-search
aliases. `dart run tool/anthropic_hosted_contract.dart` checks each spelling
against the extracted official declarations and rejects the known client tools.
This checks configuration coverage, not every nested option or live workflow.

For typed code execution, use:

```dart
final hosted = anthropic.AnthropicHostedTool(
  anthropic.CodeExecutionBuiltInTool(),
);
```

Pass the resulting values through `hostedTools` on
`AnthropicNativeClient.chatModel`, `AnthropicProtocolModel`, or the SDK-backed
`AnthropicChatModel`. Hosted names must be unique and cannot shadow registered
application tool names. The runtime protects the complete tool list from
replacement by `configure`. Provider decorations such as `allowed_callers`,
`defer_loading`, `strict` and cache control can be set through configuration.

## Pauses, replay and containers

A complete `pause_turn` response yields `ModelFinished.continuation`. The core
agent stores the response before its next invocation and counts every invocation
against `maxSteps`. It continues with the ordered native content and the same
tools. It preserves the latest returned container ID from message-start or
message-delta metadata. Configuration cannot replace an inherited container ID.
These rules follow the [official server-tool lifecycle](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/server-tools).

Each pause is a checkpoint, rather than an automatic retry of a failed request.
A malformed stream, EOF, error or cancellation does not automatically dispatch
another request. The existing error and cancellation APIs still apply. Usage
accumulates across completed model invocations. With a schema, paused text is
progress and only the final response is validated as the answer. A sanitized
message snapshot closes the intermediate structured UI state without showing a
false failure. Completed structured data survives history hydration. `maxSteps` bounds invocations,
not provider-side searches, code execution, tokens or money; also configure the
provider's limits and your application budget.

If the step limit is reached while paused, the run returns `STEP_LIMIT` and keeps
its private continuation. A new run on the same owner/thread, with no new
messages and the same model/tool configuration, can explicitly continue it.
New user messages are rejected while that continuation is pending. Use a new
run ID; a recreated agent can share the same store. This is not automatic
recovery from an arbitrary process crash or an unknown external effect.

## Mixing hosted and application tools

The adapter keeps `server_tool_use` and result blocks private and never turns
them into an application call. Your ordinary tool follows its usual schema,
approval, context and result contract. A response can defer a hosted action
while your application tool waits for approval. The next user content must then
contain all of that turn's client tool results, without additional user text.
The adapter validates this shape before dispatch.

Programmatic calls from provider code execution require an explicit
`allowed_callers` opt-in on the registered application tool's provider definition.
The adapter checks the caller type and its reference to an active code-execution
call before emitting an application call. The documented `code_execution_20260521`
caller option accepts the canonical `code_execution_20260120` response tag.
Unfinished code execution requires a returned or explicitly configured container
ID; missing identity fails before local execution. Tool input validation still applies, and `needsApproval` uses the normal
approval flow. Tool-search results stay opaque. References do not install executors or grant
permissions; the runtime invokes only application tools you separately register.

## Private data and current evidence

Ordered content lives in `anthropic.messages`, cumulative metadata and containers
in `anthropic.messages.metadata`, and the configured continuation tool list in
`anthropic.messages.tools`. Keep these fields on the backend. They can contain
sensitive fetched text, opaque encrypted values, caller IDs, container IDs and
citations. `chatHydration` excludes them. Citation deltas remain on the native
text blocks for replay; this release has no public citation-rendering event.

The normalizer accepts the pinned content union, including search, fetch, code,
bash-code, text-editor-code and tool-search results plus container uploads.
Unknown top-level blocks or deltas fail explicitly. MCP, browser tools and
complete nested response semantics remain outside this integration.

Local fixtures cover typed and raw definitions, fragmented server input, opaque
results, paused turns, exact tool/container replay, programmatic caller checks,
mixed approvals, cancellation, malformed output, hydration privacy and bounds.
They do not prove model availability, real search quality, downloaded files,
container expiry, billing or live provider behavior. See
[validation](validation.md) and [the independent developer review](dx-review.md).

The [official programmatic-calling guide](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/programmatic-tool-calling)
describes caller aliases, required containers and timeout limits. Container
expiry can still reject a later continuation; application tools must implement
idempotency and reconcile external effects. No live expiry policy is certified.


# Source: docs/anthropic-parameters.md

# Anthropic Messages request fields

Generated from the [contract inventory](anthropic-api-inventory.json), pinned to official TypeScript SDK commit `ea8d7de0e47614ae71044fbf7bf12041318ba37e`. Run `node tool/interop/anthropic-inventory.mjs --write` after reviewing changes.

These dispositions describe top-level access only. Arbitrary native JSON does not validate nested unions or establish agent orchestration, model acceptance, or live behavior. The SDK adapter owns messages, execution bounds, system instructions and tools; its output schema is protected when supplied by the runtime.

| Field | Disposition | Access and limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| max_tokens | runtime-owned | Built and protected by the agent adapter; native JSON accepts caller input. |
| messages | runtime-owned | Built and protected by the agent adapter; native JSON accepts caller input. |
| system | runtime-owned | Built and protected by the agent adapter; native JSON accepts caller input. |
| tools | runtime-owned | Runtime application tools and provider-model hostedTools are built and protected by the adapter. Selected pinned hosted blocks, approvals and paused continuation have offline fixtures; full nested semantics and live behavior remain unverified. |
| model | mixed | Adapter model constructor and SDK configure; native JSON accepts caller input. |
| output_config | mixed | SDK configure; runtime output schema is protected when requested. Native JSON accepts caller input. |
| stream | runtime-owned | Agent uses SDK streaming; native client controls the request mode. |
| user_profile_id | mixed | The adapter exposes a userProfileId header; native JSON accepts this body field separately. |
| cache_control | sdk-configure | Dart SDK 9.0.1 request configure; native JSON also accepts this field. Nested agent semantics are not established. |
| container | mixed | Initial configuration uses SDK/native JSON. Returned container IDs from message-start/delta are retained privately and reused across paused and local-tool continuations; inherited IDs are protected. Live expiry and files are unverified. |
| diagnostics | sdk-configure | Dart SDK 9.0.1 request configure; native JSON also accepts this field. Nested agent semantics are not established. |
| inference_geo | sdk-configure | Dart SDK 9.0.1 request configure; native JSON also accepts this field. Nested agent semantics are not established. |
| metadata | sdk-configure | Dart SDK 9.0.1 request configure; native JSON also accepts this field. Nested agent semantics are not established. |
| service_tier | sdk-configure | Dart SDK 9.0.1 request configure; native JSON also accepts this field. Nested agent semantics are not established. |
| speed | sdk-configure | Dart SDK 9.0.1 request configure; native JSON also accepts this field. Nested agent semantics are not established. |
| stop_sequences | sdk-configure | Dart SDK 9.0.1 request configure; native JSON also accepts this field. Nested agent semantics are not established. |
| thinking | sdk-configure | Dart SDK 9.0.1 request configure; native JSON also accepts this field. Nested agent semantics are not established. |
| tool_choice | sdk-configure | Dart SDK 9.0.1 request configure; native JSON also accepts this field. Nested agent semantics are not established. |
| workspace_id | native-json | Native JSON accepts this field; SDK configure support depends on the Dart SDK version. Agent semantics are not established. |

The inventory follows selected local type references for Messages requests, responses and stream events. Imported declarations and unrelated endpoints are outside its scope. Review protocol behavior and provider documentation separately.


# Source: docs/anthropic-computer.md

# Anthropic computer use

`AnthropicComputerTool` connects Anthropic's `computer_toolset_20260801` calls
to a desktop driver you provide. AgentWeave does not provide the desktop or
operate it itself. The [executable example](https://github.com/seifalmotaz/agent-weave/blob/main/examples/anthropic_computer_demo.dart)
uses the native Messages client, an application-owned HTTPS driver and a console
approval for each requested turn. It makes billable Anthropic requests when run.
Choose a model that supports the toolset using the [official computer-use
documentation](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/computer-use-tool).

Set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`, `COMPUTER_DRIVER_URL`,
`COMPUTER_DRIVER_TOKEN` and `COMPUTER_ENVIRONMENT_ID` in the backend
environment. Run `dart run examples/anthropic_computer_demo.dart "your task"`.
The sample uses the default in-memory run store and fixed local owner and thread
identifiers; it is a single-process demonstration, not durable or multi-user
storage. Production applications must authenticate owners, protect private
conversation state, and configure a suitable store and approval interface.
The console prints action arguments for review, which may contain sensitive data.

## Complete CLI example

Optionally set `ANTHROPIC_VERSION` to select a supported API version.

```dart
import 'dart:convert';
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:agent_weave/agent_weave.dart';
import 'package:agent_weave_anthropic/agent_weave_anthropic.dart' as anthropic;
import 'package:agent_weave_http/agent_weave_http.dart';

String environment(String name) {
  final value = Platform.environment[name];
  if (value == null || value.trim().isEmpty) throw StateError('Set $name.');
  return value;
}

Future<void> main(List<String> args) async {
  if (args.isEmpty) throw ArgumentError('Pass the task as command arguments.');
  final driverUrl = environment('COMPUTER_DRIVER_URL');
  if (Uri.parse(driverUrl).scheme != 'https') {
    throw ArgumentError('COMPUTER_DRIVER_URL must use HTTPS.');
  }
  final driverToken = environment('COMPUTER_DRIVER_TOKEN');
  final environmentId = environment('COMPUTER_ENVIRONMENT_ID');
  final driver = JsonHttpClient(
    baseUrl: driverUrl,
    requestTimeout: const Duration(seconds: 30),
  );
  final client = anthropic.AnthropicNativeClient.withApiKey(
    apiKey: environment('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY'),
    apiVersion: Platform.environment['ANTHROPIC_VERSION'] ?? '2023-06-01',
  );
  try {
    final agent = AiAgent<void>(
      model: client.chatModel(model: environment('ANTHROPIC_MODEL')),
      tools: [
        anthropic.AnthropicComputerTool<void>(
          environmentId: environmentId,
          needsApproval: true,
          allowedCallers: const ['direct'],
          execute: (call, context) async {
            final response = await driver.sendJson(
              '/execute',
              cancellation: context.cancellation,
              prepare: () => JsonHttpRequest(
                headers: {'Authorization': 'Bearer $driverToken'},
                body: {
                  'environment_id': environmentId,
                  'tool_call_id': context.toolCallId,
                  'idempotency_key': context.idempotencyKey,
                  'call': call.raw,
                },
              ),
            );
            final value = jsonDecode(response.body);
            if (value is! Map<String, dynamic>) {
              throw const FormatException('Expected a driver result object.');
            }
            return anthropic.AnthropicComputerResult.fromJson(value);
          },
        ),
      ],
    );
    var sequence = 0;
    var result = await agent.generate(
      ChatRequest(
        threadId: 'computer-demo',
        runId: 'run-${sequence++}',
        messages: [ChatMessage.user(args.join(' '), id: 'user')],
      ),
      ownerId: 'local-user',
      context: null,
    );
    while (result.status == RunStatus.interrupted) {
      stdout.writeln('Requested actions:');
      for (final interrupt in result.interrupts) {
        stdout.writeln(jsonEncode(interrupt.call.toJson()));
      }
      stdout.write('Approve this turn? [y/N] ');
      final approve = stdin.readLineSync()?.trim().toLowerCase() == 'y';
      final previous = result;
      result = await agent.generate(
        ChatRequest(
          threadId: previous.threadId,
          runId: 'run-${sequence++}',
          parentRunId: previous.runId,
          resume: [
            for (final interrupt in previous.interrupts)
              approve ? interrupt.approve() : interrupt.reject(),
          ],
        ),
        ownerId: 'local-user',
        context: null,
      );
    }
    stdout.writeln(result.text);
  } finally {
    driver.close();
    client.close();
  }
}
```

## Typed actions

The callback receives a sealed `AnthropicComputerAction`. Points are named
Dart records with `x` and `y`; regions have `x0`, `y0`, `x1`, and `y1`.
Scroll direction and click/empty-action kinds are enums. `call.raw` retains the
validated wire shape for a remote driver. Unknown input fields fail before execution.

| Action type | Values |
| --- | --- |
| `AnthropicComputerKey` | `text`, optional `repeat` |
| `AnthropicComputerHoldKey` | `text`, `duration` |
| `AnthropicComputerType` | `text` |
| `AnthropicComputerEmptyAction` | Screenshot, cursor position, mouse down/up `kind` |
| `AnthropicComputerMove` | `coordinate` point |
| `AnthropicComputerClickAction` | Click `kind`, optional `coordinate` and modifier `text` |
| `AnthropicComputerDrag` | `startCoordinate`, `coordinate`, optional modifier `text` |
| `AnthropicComputerScroll` | `amount`, `direction`, optional `coordinate` and modifier `text` |
| `AnthropicComputerWait` | `duration` |
| `AnthropicComputerZoom` | `region` |

Success from screenshot or zoom requires an image result; cursor position
requires nonempty text. Return a typed error for an action that failed. Image
contents and the truth of reported coordinates remain the driver's responsibility.

## Driver contract

The sample sends a JSON POST to `/execute` on your HTTPS driver. It sends a
bearer token, uses a 30-second timeout and passes the run cancellation token;
redirects and automatic retries are disabled. The request contains:

```json
{
  "environment_id": "desktop-1",
  "tool_call_id": "toolu_example",
  "idempotency_key": "stable-per-owner-thread-and-call",
  "call": {"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_example","toolset_name":"computer","name":"screenshot","input":{}}
}
```

Your driver must authenticate the request, bind `environment_id` to the
approved isolated desktop, validate inputs and deduplicate effects using the
idempotency key. Cancellation or timeout does not undo an action already
accepted by the driver. The driver returns an object with `content`, a list of
Anthropic text and image blocks, and optional boolean `is_error`. For example,
`{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Clicked."}]}` is an acknowledgement;
a failure can be `{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Action failed."}],"is_error":true}`.
For screenshot and zoom, return an image block, for example with a base64 PNG
source. `AnthropicComputerResult.fromJson` validates this response before the
runtime forwards it. A thrown driver/transport/decoding exception fails the
run; returning `is_error: true` reports a tool failure to Claude so it can
continue.

The runtime executes computer actions in order. After a computer result marks
an error, later executors in that turn do not run. Computer members receive the
prescribed skipped error; ordinary functions receive a generic skipped error.
The next model turn can recover from those results. By default, a turn containing a
computer action requires approval for the whole batch; native call arguments
are read-only. If approval is declined, the application must start a new thread
rather than execute the rejected native turn.

After a pause, recheck the target and current screen before applying approved actions.

The driver owns coordinate validation and conversion, screenshot capture,
image sizing and desktop isolation. Coordinates refer to full screenshots,
including after zoom; AgentWeave does not scale them. Check bounds against the
actual screenshot and enforce action limits before operating the desktop.
For documented action fields, limits, result rules and the pinned SDK projection,
see the [computer contract inventory](anthropic-computer-parameters.md).

Raw native Messages document blocks support provider file IDs in the agent;
the SDK-backed typed `configure` path still cannot decode those IDs until the
upstream SDK change is released. Neither the example nor the contract inventory
establishes live model compatibility or verifies your driver.


# Source: docs/anthropic-computer-parameters.md

# Anthropic computer toolset contract

Generated from the [inventory](anthropic-computer-inventory.json), pinned to official TypeScript SDK commit `ea8d7de0e47614ae71044fbf7bf12041318ba37e`. Run `node tool/interop/anthropic-computer-inventory.mjs --write` after review. See the [computer use documentation](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/computer-use-tool) and [SDK driver guidance](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/browser-use-sdk).

The 17 member calls use `toolset_name: computer`, the member name, and member-specific input with no action field. Dispatch by both names. Configs are sparse: each member defaults to enabled with defer_loading false. The toolset accepts cache_control. The documentation additionally permits allowed_callers with only ["direct"]; the pinned SDK declaration omits that field.

Run a batch sequentially. On failure, return an error for that action and for every subsequent unexecuted action, with the exact halt text in the inventory. Return one result for every call with its tool_use_id and toolset_name. Screenshot and zoom return an image; cursor_position returns coordinates as text. Coordinates always refer to the full screenshot, including after zoom.

The driver owns validation, coordinate conversion, image sizing, environment isolation and approval policy. Documentation specifies key repeat 1–100 (default 1), and hold_key and wait duration up to 300 seconds; the official driver guidance leaves these checks to applications. AgentWeave validates selected repeat and duration bounds before invoking the executor. These declarations and offline fixtures do not demonstrate model acceptance, desktop execution, or live behavior.


# Source: docs/ollama.md

# Ollama

Connect AgentWeave to an existing Ollama server and an installed model. Install `agent_weave`, `agent_weave_ollama`, and their dependencies in your Dart project. Set `OLLAMA_MODEL` to an installed model that supports JSON Schema; optionally set `OLLAMA_BASE_URL` (defaults to `http://localhost:11434`). Then run `dart run examples/ollama_demo.dart` from this repository.

```dart
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:agent_weave/agent_weave.dart' as weave;
import 'package:agent_weave_ollama/agent_weave_ollama.dart' as ollama;

Future<void> main() async {
  final modelId = Platform.environment['OLLAMA_MODEL'];
  if (modelId == null || modelId.isEmpty) {
    stderr.writeln(
      'Set OLLAMA_MODEL to an installed model that supports JSON schema.',
    );
    exitCode = 64;
    return;
  }
  final client = ollama.OllamaNativeClient(
    baseUrl:
        Platform.environment['OLLAMA_BASE_URL'] ?? 'http://localhost:11434',
  );
  try {
    final model = client.chatModel(
      model: modelId,
      options: const ollama.ModelOptions(temperature: 0.2),
    );
    final result = await weave.generateObject<String>(
      model: model,
      prompt: 'Give a short name for a friendly robot.',
      schema: {
        'type': 'object',
        'properties': {
          'name': {'type': 'string'},
        },
        'required': ['name'],
        'additionalProperties': false,
      },
      decode: (json) => (json as Map<String, Object?>)['name'] as String,
    );
    print(result.value);
  } finally {
    client.close();
  }
}
```

This client talks to an Ollama HTTP server; it does not run inference inside the Dart or Flutter app. On a phone, `localhost` means the phone itself, so configure a reachable server URL. Device networking and model capabilities vary and have not been verified here.

`OllamaChatModel` supports AgentWeave function tools and structured output, subject to the model's capabilities. AgentWeave validates tool arguments and applies configured approval rules before execution. Assistant thinking and native tool calls are preserved for continuation in private provider data. Ollama may return native call IDs; AgentWeave generates separate local IDs and binds tool results to the original call. When the native ID is absent, replay uses the tool name without inventing an ID on the wire. Private replay, raw frames, response metadata and logprobs can contain sensitive information; do not expose them to end users or logs.

In the pinned Ollama server, its generic parser and reviewed built-in parsers allocate increasing call indices across a response. This is not guaranteed for remote or older servers. AgentWeave accepts repeated identical indexed calls once and rejects conflicting repeats rather than guessing how to merge them. Use `streamChat` directly for protocols that need different handling.

For images, use an AgentWeave `ImagePart` containing an inline `data:image/...;base64,...` URL. Remote image URLs are not fetched. Files, audio, video and native provider-specific tool kinds are unsupported in normalized chat. The native API remains available when the model or server needs a different request shape.

The package re-exports `ollama_dart` 4.0.0 types for typed options, including `ModelOptions`, `ThinkValue`, `KeepAlive` and `EmbedRequest`. The example leaves thinking and keep-alive at server defaults. When supported by your model and desired, pass `think: const ollama.ThinkValue.enabled(true)` or `keepAlive: const ollama.KeepAlive.duration('5m')` to `client.chatModel`. Model options remain model-dependent. `maxOutputTokens` owns `options.num_predict`; `configure` cannot replace runtime-owned model, messages, tools, stream, output schema or output limit.

To embed with an installed embedding-capable model, use `OllamaEmbeddingModel(client).embed(ollama.EmbedRequest(model: embeddingModelId, input: ollama.EmbedInput.list(['first', 'second'])))`. Its result exposes immutable vectors, the raw response, the reported model and input token count. Do not assume every chat model supports embeddings.

For native JSON, use `createChat`, `createGenerate`, `embed`, `show`, or `send`; `streamChat` and `streamGenerate` expose NDJSON frames. The native client accepts a `CancellationToken` and cancels its request on cancellation or stream unsubscribe; these guarantees belong to AgentWeave's transport, not the re-exported SDK. It does not retry, pull or download models. For protected servers, supply an optional `credentialResolver` on the backend; it is called per request, permitting rotation. Diagnostic errors redact the resolved credential, but raw successful data can still be sensitive. Keep credentials off frontend clients.

Token usage and cache counts are reported only when returned by Ollama; durations and other terminal fields remain in private metadata, with full raw frames retained separately. Their presence does not guarantee caching or any model-specific behavior. Consult [the parameter inventory](ollama-parameters.md) for the pinned official schema, nested fields, source gaps and scope. A raw field being forwarded does not imply normalized runtime support. Fixture tests and compilation do not establish live model or device behavior.


# Source: docs/ollama-parameters.md

# Ollama API parameter inventory

The [official OpenAPI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/e9fde36d75fea66579d84099956ce1430792737a/docs/openapi.yaml) and [Go API types](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/e9fde36d75fea66579d84099956ce1430792737a/api/types.go) are pinned at `e9fde36d75fea66579d84099956ce1430792737a` under MIT. The [machine-readable inventory](ollama-api-inventory.json) records selected operations and nested schema fields, union shapes, and reviewed Go-only additions. The OpenAPI can lag the server types: for example, it omits message `thinking`, `tool_name`, `tool_call_id`, and tool call `id` and `function.index`. Neither source establishes model-specific support.

Agent chat owns model, messages, tools and stream construction and maps selected text and tool events. Raw native access handles other fields; agent chat retains raw frames, including logprobs, and terminal metadata in private provider output, without dedicated normalized events for every field. Generate, embed and show have no automatic agent execution. Check the implementation and tests for the actual extent of raw access; inventory is source coverage, not live verification.

Chat and generate stream **newline-delimited JSON**, not SSE; stream defaults to true. Embed and show return JSON. Image bytes are base64 strings in JSON. Go types allow embed input as text, batches, or multimodal text/image/audio maps; audio and image blobs are base64. The `format` union includes `json` or a JSON schema object; `think` is boolean or a model-defined string. `keep_alive` accepts seconds or a Go duration string; negative means keep loaded, zero unloads. Duration metrics are nanoseconds; `prompt_eval_cached_count` is a reported metric, not a cache setting.

Chat history may include assistant thinking, tool calls, tool result `tool_name` and `tool_call_id`. Tool-call `id` is optional; `function.index` is an integer and arguments are an object. Responses may contain part of a message; the pinned types do not define a universal merge rule for repeated call fragments. Preserve raw events and avoid assuming that a repeated index always represents an appendable delta.

Run `python3 tool/ollama_contract.py --check` offline; `--upstream` compares the official current source bytes without changing the pin. The OpenAPI JSON snapshot is a parsed representation of the retained YAML. Review both source diffs, update the JSON snapshot, fixtures and dispositions before refreshing. No model download or live model call is required.


# Source: docs/dart-frog.md

# Dart Frog

`agent_weave_dart_frog` exposes native Dart Frog handlers for streaming chat,
owner-scoped history, and typed generation. Add `agent_weave`,
`agent_weave_dart_frog`, and `dart_frog` to your application dependencies.

The following complete example runs without a provider key:

```dart
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:agent_weave/agent_weave.dart';
import 'package:agent_weave_dart_frog/agent_weave_dart_frog.dart';
import 'package:dart_frog/dart_frog.dart';

Future<void> main() async {
  final token = Platform.environment['DEMO_TOKEN'];
  if (token == null || token.isEmpty) {
    stderr.writeln('Set DEMO_TOKEN to run this local demonstration.');
    exitCode = 1;
    return;
  }
  final handler = chatHandler<void>(
    agent: AiAgent<void>(model: const OfflineModel()),
    authenticate: (context) =>
        context.request.headers['authorization'] == 'Bearer $token'
        ? (ownerId: 'demo-user', context: null)
        : null,
  );
  final server = await serve(handler, InternetAddress.loopbackIPv4, 8080);
  print('Demo listening at http://${server.address.address}:${server.port}');
}

final class OfflineModel implements ChatModel {
  const OfflineModel();
  @override
  ModelCapabilities get capabilities => const ModelCapabilities();
  @override
  Stream<ModelEvent> stream(
    ModelRequest request, {
    required CancellationToken cancellation,
  }) async* {
    cancellation.throwIfCancelled();
    yield const TextDelta('Hello from the offline Dart Frog example.');
    yield const ModelFinished();
  }
}
```

For an existing Dart Frog application, return the handler's response from your route. Authentication must
verify the request and supply the owner from trusted server-side identity, not
from JSON. The handler accepts POST chat requests and GET history using
`?threadId=...`, with optional `limit` and `before`. Reconnect to a run
with `?runId=...&offset=...` to replay events after a sequence. The streaming response
uses server-sent events. Cancellation follows the Dart stream subscription;
network disconnect detection depends on the HTTP server and intermediaries.

For typed generation, use `generationHandler<C, P, R>` with a
`GenerationTask<P, R>`, the same authentication callback, and a `decode`
function that receives both request parameters and the trusted authenticated
context: `decode: (input, context) => ...`. Use the context to bind any
user-specific parameters rather than trusting identity fields in the body. Both
handlers limit request bodies to 1 MiB
by default; configure `maxRequestBytes` when needed.

Run the offline example from the workspace root:

```sh
DEMO_TOKEN=local-example dart run examples/dart_frog/server.dart
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer local-example' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"threadId":"demo","runId":"first","messages":[{"id":"u1","role":"user","content":"Hello"}]}' \
  http://127.0.0.1:8080/
```

The fixed token and fixed owner are for local demonstration only, not production
authentication. The default in-memory store is process-local and is not durable.

Your application owns the agent, store, and provider client lifetimes. Keep any
authenticated context resources valid until the response stream finishes.
Close shared provider clients when the application shuts down.


# Source: docs/openai-options-audit.md

# OpenAI options audit

Historical baseline audit (see updates below): `agent_weave_openai` and installed `openai_dart` 11.0.1, compared with the [Responses API](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/responses/create), [computer-use guide](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/tools-computer-use), and [Realtime API](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/realtime). This is a source review, not an exhaustive certification of all OpenAI endpoints or individual nested SDK fields. No live API calls were made. SDK types or raw HTTP access do not imply AgentWeave orchestration or a working end-to-end feature.

| Area | SDK and adapter coverage | Gap and priority |
|---|---|---|
