| Canonical request | `chat_models.dart:90–118,203–275` maps runtime messages, tools, instructions, token limit and output schema; typed `configure` can replace the whole request. | **P0:** replacement can silently erase or alter runtime messages, tool definitions, schema, and Responses encrypted-reasoning include. Define ownership and merge rules, preserve canonical inputs/tools, and test multiple turns and callback conflicts. Changing model also makes emitted usage report the constructor model, not necessarily the actual model. |
| Responses options | SDK `CreateResponseRequest` includes model/input, instructions, tools/tool choice, previous response ID, max output/tool calls, temperature/top-p/penalties, reasoning/text, truncation/context management, parallel calls, service tier, metadata, include/store/background, safety/moderation, cache key/options/retention, top logprobs, multi-agent and access programs. Callback can set SDK-supported fields. | **P1:** options are not first-class runtime semantics; callback can conflict with canonical history and can overwrite required includes. SDK `createStream` forces `stream=true`; adapter never passes `beta=true`, required by SDK for multi-agent. Background and prior-response state need explicit lifecycle and duplicate-history rules. Check server/model constraints. |
| Responses events | `chat_models.dart:124–172` handles text/refusal/reasoning-summary deltas, completed function calls, final output and token usage. Full completed output is saved as provider replay. | **P0:** only `function_call` becomes a runnable `ToolCallReady`; computer, custom, shell, apply-patch and approval continuations are not dispatched. All tool messages become `function_call_output`. Hosted-tool events and results are retained for replay only and are not surfaced as typed progress/results. Refusals lose their distinction, incomplete causes collapse to length, errors lose details, and no terminal event is required before stream EOF. Preserve IDs, statuses, annotations, errors, incremental events and output kinds. |
| Computer use | SDK parses `computer_call` output (`models/responses/items/output_item.dart`); callback can configure SDK tool types. | **P0:** no action executor, screenshot result, safety-check acknowledgement or correct `computer_call_output` continuation in runtime. SDK `items/item.dart` dispatch does not list `computer_call_output`: verify its round trip and contribute a typed input item upstream if missing. Raw JSON sent independently is not an AgentWeave computer loop. Explicit authorization and sandbox controls belong at the execution boundary. |
| Function tools | Runtime tool schemas and JSON-object arguments are mapped; tool calls are dispatched. | **P1:** `strict:false` is fixed, arguments are assumed JSON objects, output is text only, and per-tool provider options are absent. Validate schema/arguments, preserve tool IDs and correctly represent multimodal and non-function results. Hosted tools need not be run locally. |
| Cache and state | SDK supports `prompt_cache_key`, options and retention; adapter reports `cached_tokens` if usage is present. Responses defaults to `store:false`, includes encrypted reasoning, and replays completed output. | **P1:** setting a key is not evidence of a cache hit; no cache hit/miss diagnostics or cache lifetime validation. Changing `include` can drop encrypted reasoning. `store`, `previous_response_id`, conversation state, deletion and retrieval have privacy and replay implications; test exact outgoing payloads and cache usage with an authorized live run. See [prompt caching](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/prompt-caching). |
| Query and transport | SDK `responses.retrieve` and input-item `list` accept typed `include[]` and pagination; `platform_api.dart` supports JSON, binary GET, repeated query keys, idempotency and cancellation with client interceptor chain. | **P1:** these are separate SDK/raw operations, not run lifecycle integration. Raw helper now supports GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE/HEAD, per-request safe headers, arbitrary JSON roots, response status/headers/bytes, and repeated queries for downloads. Multipart upload and arbitrary SSE remain outside this helper. Typed stream exposes abort and beta but adapter exposes only abort. Provide per-request transport options without compromising auth, retry, secret redaction or canonical request ownership. |
| Chat completions | SDK request exposes sampling, penalties, logit bias/logprobs, n, stop, tools, output format, audio/modalities, prediction, search, caching, safety, metadata/store and more through callback. | **P1:** `chat_models.dart:297–318` ignores choices other than index 0; audio output, logprobs and other deltas are not emitted, even when enabled. Either support each requested output or reject unsupported configurations; test `n`, audio and tool streaming. File and video input are explicitly rejected. |
| Images/audio/embeddings/video | `generation_models.dart` forwards SDK request objects for image generation, speech, transcription, embeddings, decision and video. Speech/transcription streaming and image streaming exist. `generation_tasks.dart` normalizes image, speech and transcription results. | **P1:** forwarding only covers fields represented by the pinned SDK; normalized tasks drop provider-specific metadata (including transcription detail) and create local IDs. Image nonstream and video create cannot abort in-flight through these wrappers; cancellation of local video waiting does not cancel a server job. Image edits/variations, translation and job operations remain direct SDK/raw workflows. Audit individual request serialization and response fields before claiming all media options. |
| Realtime | `OpenAIRealtimeModel` passes a typed session config including audio, modalities, tools, reasoning, tracing, truncation and include to SDK connection; caller owns returned session. | **P1:** this is connection access, not runtime event, tool, interruption or voice orchestration. Connection cancellation is checked before and after connect rather than aborting the handshake; session lifetime is caller-owned. WebRTC, SIP, client secrets and raw realtime events require separate SDK/API paths and their own verification. |
| API surface and future fields | Public package exports SDK surfaces; raw helper can address additional JSON endpoints. | **P2:** typed parsing may reject or drop unknown fields, while raw path has transport and response restrictions above. Inventory each endpoint, parameter, nested union and event against a dated official spec; test unknown enum/item handling. Contribute missing fields upstream rather than presenting reexports as complete integration. |

## Verification and proposed sequence

1. Add fixture-based request/stream tests proving canonical messages and tools survive configuration, required includes are merged, usage identifies the actual model, and unsupported combinations fail visibly. Cover cancellation, EOF, incomplete/failure causes, `n > 1`, cache options and repeated query keys.
2. Design typed provider events and continuation items before implementing each client-executed tool loop. Verify call IDs, multiple actions, screenshot content and safety acknowledgements across at least two turns; separately expose hosted-tool results and approvals. Keep side-effectful execution opt-in and constrained by caller policy.
3. Expose response-state and request transport controls with explicit storage, replay and retry semantics. Test retrieve/list query encoding, background lifecycle, and redaction using mock HTTP.
4. Audit every media/realtime SDK request and output union against the official endpoint schema, then add serialization and event round-trip fixtures for each claimed field. Submit reproducible upstream issues or patches for confirmed SDK omissions; preserve compatibility with the pinned version.
5. Only after fixture coverage, run separately authorized, cost-bounded live scenarios for real model/tool capability, cache metrics, media and realtime. Unit fixtures establish serialization and orchestration, not server behavior, model support or actual cache hits.

Existing tests in `packages/agent_weave_openai/test` use fixtures and cover selected text, function-call, generation, transport and cancellation paths. This audit did not run them or establish exhaustive coverage.

## Update: current worktree

The current `chat_models.dart` now guards runtime-owned messages/input and token limits, requires each runtime tool exactly once, and protects an existing runtime output schema; it merges `reasoning.encrypted_content` into Responses `include`. Usage reports only an actual model returned in the stream; it does not guess the requested alias when the provider omits identity. Fixture tests in `chat_models_test.dart` cover rejected conversation replacement, include merging, cache key/metadata serialization, and Responses returned-model usage. These changes supersede the corresponding earlier P0 request-replacement and P1 include/model findings; they do not establish exhaustive configuration coverage or live behavior. The other non-function tool continuation gaps remained open at that point; see the computer update below. The guard only compares runtime fields present in the canonical JSON and permits additional provider tools; audit individual conflicting settings before claiming full option safety.

The current raw transport fixtures verify request-specific safe headers, repeated
queries on binary downloads, raw status/headers/bytes, arbitrary JSON root
values, authenticated PUT requests, pre-cancellation and mutation retry policy.
This raw helper does not implement SSE or multipart; the separate Responses adapter handles selected computer orchestration as described below.

## Computer-use SDK contribution

[Upstream PR #430](https://github.com/davidmigloz/ai_clients_dart/pull/430) adds
typed computer-call input replay and screenshot results, including returned-only
statuses and redacted screenshots. Local upstream validation passed 25,235 unit
tests with 3 skips plus package analysis. The PR is submitted, not merged or
released. AgentWeave still uses its published SDK dependency. Shell/custom/patch calls and
MCP approval continuations remain unsupported; selected native computer use is
now integrated as described below.

## Protocol reuse and Chat continuation

The current SDK facades delegate canonical encoding and normalization to reusable
protocol models. Chat assistant history now uses text or null as required by the
SDK request type; two-turn tool continuation previously failed before dispatch
because assistant content was encoded as a user-style parts list. Protocol and
actual SDK transport regressions now exercise the second request.

Chat explicitly rejects multiple choices and requested audio output instead of
silently dropping unsupported results. Responses requires a terminal event before
EOF. These supersede the corresponding silent-drop/EOF observations above;
remaining event and media gaps are still open.

## Selected native computer integration

`OpenAIComputerTool` registers an application-executed native computer tool with
`OpenAIResponsesModel`, including the GA and legacy preview definitions. The
runtime validates completed calls, preserves action order, pauses for approval as
configured and whenever safety checks are present, and returns the application's
fresh screenshot with the matching `call_id`. Arguments are immutable and native
approval cannot edit them. The environment binding must remain stable across a
pause. Denial, cancellation, or executor failure closes the continuation with
its audit history intact; an application must not invent a computer result to
continue it. The application owns the actual driver, permissions and side effects.

This is selected computer orchestration, not support for other native tool kinds
or client-executed native tools. The [computer guide](computer-use.md) describes
the driver contract and its operational limits. Offline contract fixtures do not
prove live model or server behavior, including GA safety acknowledgements.

The Responses facade consumes raw SSE JSON through the SDK transport before
typed event decoding. This preserves original private item fields for replay and
lets the computer validator reject unknown action fields before execution.


# Source: docs/provider-coverage.md

# Provider coverage and roadmap

Status: incremental inventory, not an assertion of complete provider support. Reviewed the repository and linked provider documentation on 2026-11-04; provider APIs, models and SDK versions change. No paid calls or external mutations were made. The goal is to account for **all** options on each explicitly supported API, including nested fields, transport and lifecycle semantics; the table is a starting point rather than a complete field inventory.

## What exists

The workspace has `agent_weave_openai` backed by `openai_dart` 11.0.1, plus the `ChatModel` extension interface (`docs/providers.md`). The `agent_weave_anthropic` package has native JSON/SSE transport and a lossless Messages normalizer, plus an SDK-backed facade using `anthropic_sdk_dart 9.0.1`, with offline fixtures. The `agent_weave_openrouter` package has a native JSON transport, separate Chat and stateless Responses adapters, native options and offline fixtures. The `agent_weave_together` package provides native Chat Completions and offline fixtures. The Vercel Gateway package implements public Chat and Responses adapters with offline fixtures. The Cloudflare package implements selected native Workers AI, Gateway run, and compatible Chat and Responses contracts with offline fixtures. `OpenAIChatModel` maps runtime history and function tools to streamed Chat Completions and supports a typed SDK `configure` callback. OpenAI-compatible base URLs can be supplied through the SDK client, but neither this configuration nor custom provider support establishes endpoint-specific compatibility. Runtime currently interprets only part of the returned stream, as documented in [the OpenAI audit](openai-options-audit.md). `OpenAIPlatformApi` is a restricted JSON/raw transport, not a complete native or streaming provider adapter.

| Provider and API | What the repo implements | Significant missing work and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OpenAI native Responses and Chat | Dedicated SDK-backed adapter, selected generation/media wrappers and typed options; Responses also supports the application-executed native computer tool. | See [OpenAI audit](openai-options-audit.md): other native tool continuations, events, transport, media and complete field-by-field coverage remain open. Computer model and driver behavior require separate live verification. |
| Anthropic native Messages | Native JSON/SSE client with request options, rotating credentials, deadlines and cancellation; a guarded Messages normalizer retains unknown fields on supported blocks, signed thinking, private citations and cumulative usage. The typed SDK facade remains available. | The [inventory](anthropic-parameters.md) classifies 19 request fields and follows selected nested declarations. The 17-member application-executed computer toolset and scoped file-ID documents are integrated. Pinned hosted result blocks, bounded paused turns and container reuse now have offline integration fixtures. Complete nested semantics, browser/MCP tools, other endpoint workflows and live hosted behavior remain incomplete. Raw access and SDK exports do not establish those integrations. See [Anthropic](anthropic.md). |
| OpenRouter Chat and Responses | Native JSON/SSE client, separate Chat and stateless Responses adapters, selected typed provider/routing/reasoning/cache/plugin options and immutable native extensions. Private ordered reasoning replay and actual provider/usage/cost metadata are retained; raw envelopes remain accessible. | The [inventory](openrouter-api-reference.md) records all 146 pinned operations. Only Chat and Responses have selected integrations; management, background jobs, all hosted tools/media and exhaustive fragment/model behavior remain incomplete. Fixtures are not live billing, routing or cache evidence. See [OpenRouter](openrouter.md). |
| Together Chat Completions | Native JSON client and agent adapter, typed options, and offline request and streaming fixtures. The [chat inventory](together-chat-inventory.json) records the disposition of 27 pinned request fields. | The inventory is not complete API or model certification. Native-only fields include multiple choices and legacy function calls. Media and schema acceptance, billing, live cancellation, and live Together behavior remain unverified. See [Together](together.md). |
| Vercel AI Gateway | Public Chat Completions and Responses adapters, typed routing options, raw native JSON and event envelopes, and offline fixtures. | Selected request serialization and stream behavior do not prove live provider semantics, cost, or exhaustive API coverage. Provider identity is not inferred. The internal AI SDK V4 wire protocol is separate. See [Vercel AI Gateway](vercel-gateway.md). |
| Cloudflare Workers AI / AI Gateway | Native run, model discovery and selected embedding, transcription, image and traditional chat adapters; Gateway run and compatible Chat and Responses. | Model-specific schemas, availability, live acceptance, caching, binary audio and billing remain unverified. Native traditional tool continuation covers the documented Hermes single-call format only. See [Cloudflare](cloudflare.md). |
| Ollama native local API | Native JSON/NDJSON chat and generate transport, agent chat with thinking/tool replay, typed SDK options and embeddings. The [inventory](ollama-parameters.md) covers four selected operations and reviewed Go-only fields. | No real daemon, downloaded model or Flutter device has been tested. Model availability, remote/legacy tool fragment rules, other endpoints and exhaustive option semantics remain unverified. See [Ollama](ollama.md). |
| Other providers | Custom `ChatModel` can be implemented by users. | No blanket support or parity claim. Add named provider/API/version inventory entries and evidence before advertising them. Model availability, feature support and defaults are not stable constants. |

## Architecture requirements

1. Key capabilities by **provider, API protocol, endpoint and model**, distinguishing supported, unsupported and unknown. Do not advertise unconditional tools, media or structured output for every model. Preserve the core runtime's authoritative conversation and registered tools while allowing explicit provider options; reject incompatible combinations rather than silently ignoring them.
2. Reuse an actively maintained typed Dart SDK when it actually represents the endpoint and preserves required fields. `openai_dart` is already useful for OpenAI and the subset of compatible wire formats its request types model; it is not an Anthropic SDK or proof of arbitrary extension support. Evaluate candidate native SDK maintenance, license, streaming, cancellation, types, unknown fields and release cadence before adoption. Where a specific field or union is missing, reproduce the omission against official docs and submit a focused upstream issue or patch with serialization and round-trip tests; do not fork preemptively.
3. Define explicit provider-specific typed options plus a controlled forward-compatible extension mechanism where transport supports it. Separate request fields, query parameters, request-scoped headers, multipart/binary data and SSE/WebSocket transport; preserve auth, cancellation, timeouts and safe retry/idempotency semantics. Never log credentials or sensitive replay blocks. An escape hatch alone does not implement orchestration.
4. Preserve raw provider continuation privately and round-trip every relevant block in order. Map function calls, application-executed computer calls, other native and hosted tools, approvals, tool results and IDs distinctly; do not force all results into a function-output schema. Preserve refusal, errors, finish reasons, structured output, citations, reasoning, media, cache and usage/provider metadata without presenting private continuation as UI text.
5. Inventory all create/retrieve/list/delete/cancel/query operations, paging, background jobs, cache and storage settings, file/media upload, realtime and model-specific limits separately. Make explicit whether each is typed SDK access, raw escape hatch, integrated runtime behavior, fixture-verified or live-verified.

## Verification and upkeep

- Maintain a versioned machine-readable inventory per provider/API/endpoint: official source URL and revision/date, request and response field/union, defaults, constraints, SDK representation, adapter handling, tests and status. Generate a human-readable coverage report and fail CI on unexplained inventory/spec changes when a reliable machine-readable spec is available; manually review provider changes where it is not.
- Offline contract fixtures must assert exact request JSON/headers/query and parse provider event sequences. Cover text, schema, fragmented parallel tool arguments, multi-turn replay, hosted vs client tools, rejection, malformed/unknown events, errors, EOF, usage, caching markers, pagination, cancellation, privacy and retry. Add endpoint-specific incompatible-option tests. Include a mock HTTP consumer scenario for each claimed compatible provider, not just SDK unit tests.
- Separately run explicitly authorized, spend-limited live smoke tests per provider/model/endpoint for text, tools, structured output, usage and any claimed media/cache behavior. Record model, date, capability, output and whether a real cache hit occurred; a fixture, reexport or HTTP 200 is not proof of real orchestration. Re-run after SDK or provider-spec changes. Do not treat this roadmap as completed until every supported surface has an inventoried, tested status and known exclusions.


# Source: docs/compatibility.md

# Compatibility

The interoperability baseline is `@tanstack/ai-client 1.0.1` and
`tanstack_ai_dart 0.4.0` at commit
`819ff289e6dabc5f424208b07ea9ac6f399cdccc`.

The root workspace pins the Dart client through a Git dependency override
because 0.4.0 was not on pub.dev when this workspace was created. Remove the
override only after checking the published package and rerunning interop tests.

## Implemented contracts

- Text streaming, standard reasoning events, and structured-output events.
- Configured server tools, client-tool pauses, and default tool approvals.
- Selected OpenAI Responses native computer calls with application-owned
  execution, safety approvals, screenshots, and continuation; see
  [computer use](computer-use.md).
- Approval, rejection, edited arguments, and continuation lineage.
- Server-owned conversation history and owner isolation.
- HTTP/SSE chat, history paging, and stored-event replay.
- Native Serverpod streaming through the existing Dart AI client.
- Generic generation progress and results, plus image/speech/transcription
  normalization helpers.

The official JavaScript test verifies text, reasoning, structured output, server tools,
default approvals, client tools, generation, and supported media input/history
round trips against a Dart HTTP server. The Dart tests exercise the client against
the runtime and a generated Serverpod endpoint over a real WebSocket. This is
not a claim of full TanStack AI core parity.

## Current limits

- Selected native computer use is implemented for OpenAI Responses and the
  Anthropic computer toolset. The application provides the actual driver. Native
  client-executed tools and other native tool kinds are unsupported; native
  approval arguments cannot be edited.
- Custom approval payload schemas, application-defined generic interrupts, subagents, MCP discovery,
  and provider-hosted tool event normalization are not implemented.
- Server tools execute sequentially. Applications can perform concurrency
  inside a tool, with their own cancellation and idempotency policy.
- Disconnecting a direct run cancels its provider request. Replaying a stored
  run does not restart it or recover execution after a server crash.
- Replay observers are bounded to 20 seconds per request. A timed-out observer
  must reconnect; the observation timeout does not cancel the original run.
- PostgreSQL is the supported persistent store. The raw SQL store does not
  claim SQLite compatibility.
- Binary artifact hosting and automatic media reconstruction after a client
  reload are not implemented. Inline results can be retained by application
  storage; provider URLs may expire.
- OpenAI resource coverage combines typed SDK delegation and an explicit raw
  JSON helper. Complete typed endpoint parity and exhaustive endpoint tests
  remain unfinished.
- Document support varies by adapter. Responses accepts URLs, inline data, and
  OpenAI file IDs. Anthropic accepts URLs, inline PDF, and inline plain text;
  native file IDs use `provider: 'anthropic'`; typed SDK configuration still
  cannot decode those handles. Gateway Responses accepts URLs and
  inline data but blocks file IDs. OpenRouter Responses also accepts URL/inline
  documents and rejects foreign file IDs. OpenRouter Chat, OpenAI Chat
  Completions, and Together reject document parts. See [documents](documents.md) for storage
  implications.
- OpenRouter has separate native Chat and stateless Responses adapters. Selected
  routing, plugin and cache options, ordered private reasoning replay and compact
  provider/cost metadata have offline fixtures. Complete management, background,
  hosted-tool and output-media integrations remain unfinished. See [OpenRouter](openrouter.md).
- Anthropic native JSON/SSE access preserves arbitrary JSON, while normalized
  chat handles selected block/delta types and the 17-member computer toolset.
  Pinned hosted blocks, bounded paused turns and container reuse are integrated
  with offline fixtures. Browser/MCP tools, live hosted behavior and complete
  nested field semantics remain unfinished. The
  SDK-backed facade retains its pinned SDK transport cancellation limits.
  See [Anthropic](anthropic.md).
- Together Chat has typed options and native JSON methods. Its agent adapter
  supports one choice; model acceptance of tools, schema, and media remains
  unverified. See [Together](together.md).
- Vercel AI Gateway supports selected Chat and Responses contracts with offline
  fixtures; provider selection, model acceptance, and billing are unverified.
  See [Vercel AI Gateway](vercel-gateway.md).
- Cloudflare supports selected native Workers AI, Gateway run, and compatible
  Chat and Responses contracts with offline fixtures. Model availability,
  acceptance and live gateway behavior are unverified. Native traditional tool
  continuation is limited to the documented Hermes single-call format. See
  [Cloudflare](cloudflare.md).
- Ollama native chat uses NDJSON with private thinking, native call ID and metadata
  replay. Typed options and embeddings are available; a real daemon, model and
  Flutter device remain untested. External image URLs are not fetched, only inline
  base64 images are accepted. Conflicting repeated tool indexes fail explicitly.
  See [Ollama](ollama.md).
- Dart Frog handlers support authenticated chat, history, replay and typed
  generation over actual local HTTP. Production authentication, reverse-proxy
  disconnects and durable restart require application-level verification. See
  [Dart Frog](dart-frog.md).
- Microphone capture, playback, WebRTC device behavior, and all provider account
  permissions require application/device testing.

These limits are release work, not hidden fallbacks. See `docs/validation.md`
and `docs/updating.md` before extending a compatibility claim.


# Source: docs/updating.md

# Update upstream dependencies

1. Record the current Dart, Serverpod, OpenAI SDK, and TanStack pins.
2. Run `python3 tool/audit_openai.py` to compare the official operation index.
   Review additions and removals before running `--refresh`.
3. Read the changed request schemas and stream-event contracts. An unchanged
   endpoint URL does not prove an unchanged contract.
4. Update provider fixtures and add a regression test for each behavior changed
   in AgentWeave. Use the provider SDK's own tests as additional evidence.
5. Update the official JavaScript client pin in `tool/interop/package.json` and
   its lockfile when changing the interoperability baseline.
6. Update the Dart client pin independently. Verify its published version before
   replacing the workspace Git override.
7. Resolve the lockfile with the minimum supported Dart SDK, then run
   `dart run tool/check.dart` on both the minimum SDK and stable. New transitive
   versions can require a newer SDK even when application constraints do not.
   Keep fixture and live results separate.
8. Update the compatibility matrix, changelogs, examples, and LLM documentation.

## Serverpod models

Use Serverpod CLI 4.1.0 while the packages target that version. Generate the
storage module before the example application:

```sh
serverpod generate --directory packages/agent_weave_serverpod_storage_server
serverpod generate --directory examples/serverpod/agent_weave_demo_server
```

Create a migration inside each affected server/module directory. Never edit
generated model or protocol files. Run real database tests after a schema or
transaction change.

## Releases

Run publication dry-runs for each package. Publish dependency packages before
their dependants. The native client currently depends on an unpublished Dart
client version, which must be resolved before publishing that package.
Create a reviewed tag and release notes that identify the tested upstream pins
and the remaining limits. A Git push is not a pub.dev publication.

## Custom store migration

`RunStore.complete` must atomically append the terminal event, save the final
checkpoint, and release the reservation. Do not implement it as two separately
committed calls. The shared contract in `test/support/run_store_contract.dart`
runs against both memory and PostgreSQL and exercises rollback and stale writers.

## Together contract snapshots

The native Together adapter is checked against a full official TypeScript SDK
commit. `tool/contracts/together/source.json` records the pin and original file
paths; unmodified reference snapshots retain their upstream license.

Run `node tool/interop/inventory.mjs --upstream` after installing the interop
tool dependencies to detect changes in the two upstream source files. This is
also part of the manually invoked upstream-review workflow. It can report
non-semantic documentation changes; review the source diff.

Select a full commit and update the snapshots before changing the pin. Review
changed field types, nested unions, stream semantics and response handling.
Update the Dart implementation, executable option fixture and `coverage.json`
dispositions, then run `node tool/interop/inventory.mjs --write` and the full
check. To reproduce the offline field check separately:

```sh
dart run tool/together_contract.dart
node tool/interop/inventory.mjs --check
```

A classified field is not evidence of model acceptance or exhaustive coverage.
Keep raw-native access, normalized agent behavior and live results distinct.

## Gateway option declarations

`tool/contracts/vercel-gateway/source.json` pins the official SDK option source
and retains its upstream license. The generated reference classifies named
options, credentials, native extensions and SDK-only fields. It is not a public
endpoint specification. Verify new options against current official HTTP docs.

```sh
node tool/interop/gateway-inventory.mjs --upstream
dart run tool/gateway_contract.dart
node tool/interop/gateway-inventory.mjs --check
```

Review any source change before updating the full commit and snapshot. Update
coverage dispositions, Dart options and fixture, then regenerate with `--write`
and run the full check. The manually invoked upstream workflow compares both
Together and Gateway sources; it does not publish packages or mutate pins.

## Cloudflare contracts

Review the [Cloudflare API reference](cloudflare-api-reference.md) and its
machine-readable inventory when provider schemas or documented contracts
change. Update the relevant implementation, fixtures, and dispositions
together. Verify model-specific schemas separately; an inventory entry does not
prove live model acceptance.

```sh
python3 tool/cloudflare_contract.py --upstream --check
python3 tool/cloudflare_contract.py --check
```

The manual upstream workflow compares the selected Cloudflare OpenAPI paths and
six public model schemas with the reviewed snapshots. It fails on drift and
never rewrites the pin. See `tool/contracts/cloudflare/README.md` for refreshing
the revision, retained licenses and operation dispositions.

## OpenRouter contracts

The OpenRouter source is a SHA-256-pinned official OpenAPI document
with a stated MIT license. Credential-shaped example values are redacted in the
retained snapshot, which has a separate hash. The updater verifies both hashes
and the deterministic transformation. Its inventory retains references and records component
fields once, avoiding repeated expansion of recursive schemas. All operations
receive an explicit status; only selected Chat/Responses behavior is integrated.

```sh
python3 tool/openrouter_contract.py --upstream --check
python3 tool/test_openrouter_contract.py
python3 tool/openrouter_contract.py --check
```

Review source drift, the field statuses, implementation and fixture behavior
together before changing the hash. New fields forwarded through native JSON
still need a disposition and tests for any claimed orchestration. See
`tool/contracts/openrouter/README.md` for provenance and retained license.

## OpenAI computer contract

`tool/contracts/openai-computer/source.json` pins the official `openai-node`
Responses declarations, with its Apache-2.0 license retained beside the source.
The inventory checks selected computer declarations and reviewed field types,
not the entire Responses API. After installing the interop tool dependencies:

```sh
dart run tool/computer_contract.dart
node --test tool/interop/computer-inventory.test.mjs
node tool/interop/computer-inventory.mjs --check
node tool/interop/computer-inventory.mjs --upstream
```

The last command compares upstream main with the pinned projection; review drift and official
provider documentation before changing the revision or regenerating the inventory.
Update the reviewed types, Dart behavior and fixtures together. These offline
checks do not establish live provider or model support.

## Anthropic Messages contract

The official TypeScript source is pinned in `tool/contracts/anthropic/source.json`.
The inventory follows request, response and stream declarations plus their local
type references. Imported types and unrelated endpoints are outside this scope.
Top-level dispositions describe access, not full nested or model semantics.

```sh
node --test tool/interop/anthropic-inventory.test.mjs
node tool/interop/anthropic-inventory.mjs --check
node tool/interop/anthropic-inventory.mjs --upstream
```

Review field and union drift before changing the pin. Update the native client,
normalizer, SDK patch preservation, request fixtures and disposition together.
New raw JSON fields do not imply the agent supports their continuation protocol.

## Anthropic computer toolset

The selected computer projection uses the existing Anthropic source pin. Its
Dart fixture serializes the actual helper, typed configs, all action parameters,
scroll enum values and result payloads. The check runs `dart` from PATH; CI uses
the selected minimum or stable SDK. The upstream-only check does not require Dart.

```sh
node --test tool/interop/anthropic-computer-inventory.test.mjs
node tool/interop/anthropic-computer-inventory.mjs --check
node tool/interop/anthropic-computer-inventory.mjs --upstream
```

Review documentation-only constraints separately, including direct callers,
numeric limits and stopping a batch after failure. The official SDK declaration
currently omits the documented `allowed_callers` field. Parameter forwarding is
not evidence of real desktop operation or complete provider support.

## Ollama native contracts

`tool/contracts/ollama` retains the official OpenAPI and Go API declarations at
the revision recorded in its README. Review both sources: the OpenAPI omits
some fields already present in the Go server types. The selected operation and
field inventory distinguishes raw access from normalized runtime behavior.

```sh
python3 tool/test_ollama_contract.py
python3 tool/ollama_contract.py --check
python3 tool/ollama_contract.py --upstream --check
```

After reviewing a new pin, update source hashes, the parsed OpenAPI snapshot,
Go-only field dispositions and runtime fixtures together. Re-run native NDJSON
transport, private replay, tool-ID/index, cancellation, embedding and independent
consumer checks. The manual upstream workflow compares official source bytes.
Do not infer model acceptance or a universal tool-fragment merge rule from the
source inventory; record actual model/version evidence separately.

## Anthropic hosted lifecycle

Run `dart run tool/anthropic_hosted_contract.dart` after regenerating the existing
Messages inventory. It exercises all pinned server-tool type spellings through
the public constructor and excludes client tools. Review content/result unions,
container metadata, allowed callers and mixed client/server continuation against
the provider docs separately. Update the hosted fixtures, core continuation
tests, PostgreSQL scenario, official-client pause cases and consumer review
together; constructor coverage is not full orchestration or live evidence.

The `code_execution_20260521` caller option alias is documented outside the
response union: the provider returns the `code_execution_20260120` caller tag.
Keep the [programmatic-calling guide](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/programmatic-tool-calling)
and both positive/negative caller fixtures in the review; a request-field pin
alone cannot prove that behavior.


# Source: docs/validation.md

# Validation

This is development version `0.1.0-dev.1`. A passing test verifies its named
scenario. It does not certify every provider endpoint or production deployment.

## Reproduce the offline checks

Requires Git, Dart 3.12.2 or later, Node.js 22 or later, npm, and Python 3.
The first run downloads dependencies and Serverpod's embedded PostgreSQL binary.
No API key is needed. Ordinary tests force the offline provider even if a key
exists in the environment.

```sh
dart pub get --enforce-lockfile
dart run tool/check.dart
```

The check includes formatting, strict static analysis, generated LLM-document
freshness, credential-pattern scanning, unit tests, PostgreSQL/network tests,
and interoperability with the pinned official JavaScript client.

## Verified locally

The latest local-model and Dart Frog increment was checked on Dart 3.12.2. The prior
147-test baseline was also checked on Dart 3.13.3.

- 391 Dart unit and regression tests: tool validation, approvals, client tools,
  lineage, cancellation, partial-response retention, safe failure history,
  generation, storage, protocol parsing, and provider fixtures.
- 16 Serverpod integration tests with a real isolated PostgreSQL database:
  authenticated endpoints, a generated-client WebSocket, HTTP/SSE, history,
  replay, owner isolation, event persistence, and reservation contention.
  The HTTP test also runs the official JavaScript client against real Serverpod
  chat and generation routes, including a second turn and persisted history.
- 19 standalone official JavaScript client scenarios against a Dart HTTP server:
  text, server tools, approvals, client tools, reasoning, structured output,
  generation, two provider-continuation cases, and seven media/history cases. The media cases include document
  URL, inline bytes, scoped and unscoped file handles, image/video URLs, and
  inline audio; returned parts pass the official AG-UI schemas.
- 4 additional official JavaScript scenarios use actual Dart Frog handlers and a
  local fake Ollama NDJSON service: text, schema, approval/resume and authenticated
  typed generation, including owner isolation, privacy and safe errors.
- 2 offline checks for the upstream operation-index parser.
- The offline chat example executes successfully.

Provider fixtures cover native Anthropic Messages and OpenAI Responses/Chat
Completions streams, schema output,
usage, opaque reasoning replay, cancellation, image/audio/embedding/Decisions/
video requests, binary and multipart transport, and the raw API helper. Realtime
uses an actual local WebSocket; it does not contact OpenAI.

CI is configured to repeat the offline checks on Dart 3.12.2 and stable on
Linux. Check the repository's current Actions run before treating that matrix
as verified.

## Live OpenAI evidence

Eight explicitly authorized requests passed on November 3–4, 2026 UTC:

| Check | Provider model | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Responses text | `gpt-5.4-nano` | Stream completed; usage returned |
| Chat Completions text | `gpt-5.4-nano` | Stream completed; usage returned |
| Structured output | `gpt-5.4-nano` | Schema-validated JSON |
| Server tool round trip | `gpt-5.4-nano` | Two invocations; tool executed and answer completed |
| Embedding | `text-embedding-3-small` | Requested vector dimensions returned |
| Image | `gpt-image-2` | One low-quality 1024×1024 image; 725,797 PNG bytes |
| Speech | `gpt-4o-mini-tts` | Short speech request; 36,044 WAV bytes |

Chat invocations reported 212 input and 51 output tokens in total. The image
reported 16 input text tokens and 196 output image tokens. Provider billing is
authoritative; these observations are not an invoice.

`tool/live_smoke.dart` and `tool/live_media_smoke.dart` are opt-in. They share
`.dart_tool/live-budget.json` and never run in CI. The ledger conservatively
reserved $2.75 across the eight requests, within the user's $5 maximum. The
current guard refuses requests beyond $4 in cumulative reservations. Actual
usage cost is much lower than those reservations. Do not reset that ledger to
bypass the cap. The guard is a bounded test allowlist, not a general billing
system. Keep keys in environment variables only.

## Package validation

The initial six-package publication dry-runs passed with zero warnings from a
clean checkout. That evidence predates the Anthropic and OpenRouter packages. The new OpenRouter
package also passed a publication dry-run with zero warnings on Dart 3.12.2. Core and OpenAI API documentation generated with zero warnings or
errors. Serverpod code generation was rerun without changing the checked-in
outputs. The native client reports
an override hint because its `tanstack_ai_dart 0.4.0` dependency is Git-pinned
in this workspace and was not published to pub.dev at validation time. Resolve
that dependency before publishing the native client. A local dry-run does not
prove that pub.dev can resolve the entire unpublished package family.

## Not verified live

No paid video jobs, realtime sessions, transcription, Decisions, administration,
storage jobs, or other delegated resources were invoked. Their local fixtures
and typed SDK access do not substitute for account-specific live tests.

Flutter device rendering, microphone permissions, audio playback, WebRTC,
production authentication, production deployment, and pub.dev publication have
not been tested or performed. See [compatibility](compatibility.md) for remaining
implementation limits.

## Native Anthropic increment

Thirteen native Messages fixture tests and a separate consumer over real loopback
HTTP verify selected text, schema, tool, thinking replay, cache configuration,
error and cooperative cancellation contracts. No live Anthropic account, model,
real cache hit or network-abort behavior was tested. The independent review is
8.0/10 for the reviewed general SDK journeys and provisionally 7.8/10 for the
new native provider path; see [the review record](dx-review.md).

## Persisted approval process restart

The isolated PostgreSQL test now starts the actual backend and approval CLI in
separate processes, exits both, starts a fresh backend against the same database
files, and restores/resolves the pending approval from a fresh client. A further
fresh client rejects the already-completed decision. The independent Terra
reviewer reran the test successfully on Dart 3.12.2 and scored this targeted
journey 8.5/10. This is graceful restart evidence, not arbitrary-crash recovery
or proof of exactly-once external effects.

## Documents and OpenRouter increment

Fifteen core document tests cover construction, validation, storage and authorized
history round trips, legacy source aliases, capability rejection, and releasing
reservations without erasing an unreadable snapshot. Provider fixtures verify
Responses URL/data/file-ID mapping and foreign-provider rejection; Anthropic PDF
URL, PDF bytes and UTF-8 text plus unsupported ID/format failures.

Three OpenRouter loopback tests verify selected routing/header options, streamed
tool arguments, actual model usage, inline errors and pre-cancellation. Two
independent consumer programs, `examples/review_cases/documents.dart` and
`examples/review_cases/openrouter.dart`, run in the normal check. The reviewed
journeys scored 8.0/10 and 7.8/10 after documentation fixes. Neither score
certifies complete provider support. No new live API calls were made.

Eighteen Together tests run a local HTTP service and cover native numeric

fragmented tool arguments with repeated IDs/names, usage after finish, bounded
text output, native metadata, multi-choice EOF, stream/HTTP errors and private
diagnostics. Cancellation is tested before sending, before response headers and
during the body. Cancelling the native stream subscription also aborts a
pending request without closing the shared client; a stalled response tests
per-request timeout. These are real
local HTTP tests, not live Together calls.

The independent consumer program exercises schema output, a stored tool approval
and continuation, reasoning/tool replay, partial output and error diagnostics.
Its targeted offline DX score remains 8/10; it does not certify production
behavior or all native fields.

The offline AST tool has three parser/coverage tests. It extracts the pinned
official SDK declarations and checks all 27 top-level chat request fields have
reviewed dispositions. An executable Dart fixture serializes every typed option.
`--upstream` was also run against current official source and found no difference
in the pinned files. No new paid requests were made.

The Together package publication dry-run passed with zero warnings on Dart
3.12.2. This is packaging evidence, not a pub.dev publication.

Seven Gateway fixtures cover separate public Chat/Responses requests, routing

and headers, credential-wait cancellation/deadlines, late-dispatch prevention,
pending-header cancellation, custom clients with stalled bodies, malformed frames,

The 28 OpenAI chat/protocol tests now include protocol and actual SDK two-turn
Chat tool continuation, assistant text/null encoding, provider replay/file-handle
isolation, explicit unsupported choices/audio, Responses EOF, and independent
subscription cancellation with a concurrent request. Three core tests cover
sticky cancellation events and disposable listeners.

The independent Gateway consumer tests both protocols through schema generation,
stored approval/resume, request credential rotation, serialized UI hydration,
wrong-provider replay exclusion and native response metadata. Both public guide
examples compile unchanged. Its documented targeted score progressed from 5.8
to 6.4 and then 7.6/10 after fixes. These are local fixtures, not a live Gateway
account, Flutter UI, secret manager, route selection, cache hit or billing test.

The five AST/coverage parser tests and executable Dart fixtures verify reviewed
Together fields and 16 named Gateway SDK options. The Gateway source type permits
unknown service options; classifying its fields does not prove a complete public
HTTP contract. No new paid provider calls were made.

Both new HTTP and Gateway package publication dry-runs passed with zero warnings
on Dart 3.12.2. Neither package has been published to pub.dev.

## Cloudflare and cancellation increment

Sixteen Cloudflare fixtures cover distinct native, Gateway and compatible wire
contracts, model-schema GET queries, embedding shape/pooling, binary and JSON
audio, binary images and decoded Flux image JSON, request snapshots, credential
rotation/redaction, approval and the documented single-call native continuation.
Raw streaming cancellation is checked after headers and a data event. Client
Gateway defaults and explicit request overrides preserve authentication.

The independent consumer exercises both compatible protocols through two-turn
tool continuation, typed media results, stored native approval, cancellation
during credential resolution and after sending, and Gateway header inheritance.
Its after-headers streaming fixture also passes over actual loopback HTTP. The
complete guide entry program was compiled unchanged, without invoking Cloudflare.
The targeted review improved from 7/10 to 8/10; it is not SDK-wide acceptance.

Twelve shared HTTP tests now include GET/HEAD with repeated queries, binary PATCH
bytes and immutable snapshots, MIME/byte validation and body/method rejection
before dispatch. Shared stream binding isolates sibling calls while synchronously
propagating parent cancellation. The full suite caught and now prevents an extra
buffered text chunk entering cancelled history. Core, provider and generation
regressions verify cleanup and independent shared-parent calls.

The Cloudflare extractor has five tests for reference closure, escaped and
recursive schema references, nested unions/constraints, and explicit operation
status. It records all 82 operations across 50 AI/Gateway paths in the pinned

The explicit upstream comparison matched current official sources. Compatible
Chat/Responses endpoints are documentation-only contracts outside that OpenAPI
revision; their separate fixtures do not certify all fields or models.

The documentation build and two routing/search tests pass. The Cloudflare package
publication dry-run has zero warnings. No package was published, no model license

## Native OpenRouter and lossless Responses replay

Fourteen OpenRouter fixtures cover native typed options and guarded JSON
extensions, ordered Chat reasoning, stateless Responses replay, raw metadata,
per-request credentials, malformed SSE, resolver errors, cancellation and client
ownership. The shared Responses codec now uses immutable raw input snapshots,
retaining reasoning and valid tool-output fields the typed input decoder could
reject or omit. Forty Chat/Responses codec tests include unknown fields,
actual SDK encrypted-reasoning replay, pre-callback canonical snapshots, missing
instructions, alternate token bounds and stream-option protections. Usage
model identity comes only from reported response data, including earlier stream
frames; it is not guessed from a requested alias. Together has the same rule.

The independent native consumer tests schema generation through both protocols,
persisted approval and resumed tools, recreated agents, opaque ordered reasoning,
IDs/statuses and matching tool outputs, no private replay in UI hydration,
actual model/provider/cost metadata, absence of usage, credential rotation,
redaction, network cancellation and borrowed-client ownership. The guide's first
program was compiled unchanged without paid execution. Its five qualitative
ratings average 7.6/10 after the guide and fixture changes. This is a targeted
review, not SDK-wide acceptance or live service evidence.

The OpenRouter source inventory accounts for 146 operations across 108 paths
and records reusable component fields without expanding recursive references
at every use. Six new extractor tests and the five Cloudflare extractor tests
pass; the refactored shared helper produces the unchanged Cloudflare inventory.
The explicit upstream OpenRouter comparison matched the pinned document hash.
Only Chat and Responses have selected integrations; other operations remain
not integrated. Source forwarding does not implement every response union or
background job.

No new paid requests or package publications were made. Live OpenRouter routing,
cache hits, cost/billing, model-specific reasoning fragments, management APIs,
hosted tools and output media remain unverified or unfinished.

OpenRouter credential-shaped source examples are deterministically redacted
before storage and generation. Original-source and retained-snapshot hashes
are verified separately. The local credential scan also checks OpenRouter key
formats and includes the full source snapshots.

## Native Anthropic transport and lossless normalization

The 37 Anthropic tests include 15 new native transport fixtures and nine new
protocol/configuration regressions. They verify request/response JSON snapshots,
version and attribution headers, repeated queries, create/count/GET access,
credential rotation and redaction, malformed/error/EOF handling, request deadlines,
pre-cancellation and cancellation during credentials, headers and stalled bodies.
Actual local HTTP tests verify independent sibling calls and borrowed-client use.

The raw normalizer preserves original fields on supported content blocks, private
citations, signed thinking, message metadata and final cumulative cache and
thinking-token usage. Typed SDK configuration changes are applied to the raw
request without erasing unchanged unknown fields. Tests reject canonical-history
mutation, absent-field injection, output-schema replacement and mismatched deltas.

The independent native consumer runs text/schema, stored approval and recreated
agent continuation, private replay and UI hydration, cache options, final usage,
citations, rotation, diagnostics, cancellation, ownership and malformed frames.
Its targeted score is 8.4/10. The guide's first program matches the example,
analyzes and compiles on Dart 3.12.2 without executing a paid request.

Four AST tests verify request field dispositions and selected nested declaration
and union drift. The inventory records 19 top-level fields and 251 locally
referenced declarations from the pinned official SDK. The current upstream
comparison matched the projection. Imported types, unrelated endpoints and
complete nested runtime semantics remain outside this evidence.

[Upstream SDK PR #432](https://github.com/davidmigloz/ai_clients_dart/pull/432)
fixes stalled-request cancellation separately. All 1,796 Anthropic SDK unit tests
passed locally with three environment-dependent skips, and package analysis was
clean. These used the locally available workspace package configuration; a clean
repository bootstrap and live tests were not run. The PR is submitted, not merged
or released, and AgentWeave's native client does not depend on it.

No live Anthropic requests or cache hits were tested, and no paid requests or
package publications were made. Hosted/browser tools, pause-turn and complete
endpoint/nested-option parity remain unfinished. Selected computer and native
file-ID integration are verified in the increment below. Provider error details retain private content after credential
scrubbing and must not be exposed directly to UI or logs.

Six core tests cover sequential native result policies, stopping mixed-turn

Two AST mutation tests and an executable Dart fixture compare 68 selected

at a time to bound test database disk use; contention tests still issue concurrent

clean rerun.

No real desktop effects, image capture, live model support or provider permissions
were verified, and no paid requests or package publication occurred. Browser and

client-result batches and explicitly opted-in programmatic callers. Hosted calls

stricter structured fixture exposed an errored intermediate placeholder despite

for intermediate structured progress and persists completed structured data.

# Source: CONTRIBUTING.md

# Contribute to AgentWeave

Open an issue or pull request with the behavior you want to change. Include a
small Dart example showing the intended developer experience.

Use Dart's recommended lints and formatter. Prefer named parameters, typed
configuration, immutable data, sealed events, and Streams. Keep provider-specific
options out of the core runtime. Do not add an abstraction without a caller.

For a bug fix, add a regression test that fails before the fix. For protocol or
provider changes, include representative request/response fixtures and explain
which upstream contract they exercise. Never commit real credentials or private
provider responses.

Run `dart run tool/check.dart` before opening a pull request. Record any check
you could not run. Paid provider tests require explicit authorization and the
existing cumulative budget ledger. Keep them out of ordinary CI.

See [updating upstream](docs/updating.md) for provider, Serverpod, and TanStack
changes. See [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for the repository map and ownership rules.


# Source: AGENTS.md

# AgentWeave

AgentWeave is an independent Dart AI runtime. It is not an official TanStack,
OpenAI, or Serverpod SDK. Preserve protocol interoperability without copying
TypeScript API conventions into the Dart developer API.

## Start here

- Read `README.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, and `docs/compatibility.md`.
- Core model contracts and agent execution live in `packages/agent_weave`.
- Provider-specific types stay in `packages/agent_weave_openai` and
  `packages/agent_weave_anthropic`, `packages/agent_weave_openrouter`, and
  `packages/agent_weave_together`, `packages/agent_weave_vercel_gateway`, and
  `packages/agent_weave_cloudflare`, and `packages/agent_weave_ollama`.
  Shared JSON HTTP transport belongs in `packages/agent_weave_http`.
  The Anthropic normalizer consumes raw events; preserve opaque block fields
  and signed thinking before SDK decoding. Typed SDK configuration must apply
  changes to a pre-callback snapshot without erasing unknown replay fields.
  Anthropic hosted tools never invoke local executors. Preserve container IDs
  and exact tools across unfinished turns. Use ModelFinished.continuation so
  checkpoints and maxSteps govern provider-owned pauses; never hide retry loops
  inside adapters. Native provider protocols require their own
  serialization, continuation, and option-preservation tests.
- HTTP/session integration lives in `packages/agent_weave_serverpod`.
  Dart Frog handlers live in `packages/agent_weave_dart_frog`.
  Ollama uses native NDJSON transport, not the compatible SSE codecs.
  Preserve native IDs privately and use distinct local tool-call IDs.
- Native client transport lives in `packages/agent_weave_serverpod_client`.
- Optional storage is a Serverpod module, `agent_weave_serverpod_storage_server`,
  with a generated `agent_weave_serverpod_storage_client`.
- The runnable backend and its real PostgreSQL/network tests live in
  `examples/serverpod/agent_weave_demo_server`.

## Rules

Use named parameters, immutable values, sealed events, patterns, and Dart
Streams. Prefer typed provider options and schema-validated tool inputs.
Use prefixes for provider imports to avoid collisions such as `Tool`.
Keep credentials on the backend and outside source control.

Authentication owns `ownerId`. Never accept it from a request body.
Validate all approval answers before invoking any tool in that batch.
Preserve run reservations, event ordering, and server-owned history.
Never automatically rerun external effects after a crash. Tools use their
`idempotencyKey` to implement idempotency with the destination service.

Never edit generated protocol/model files. Change `.spy.yaml` or endpoint
sources, then run Serverpod 4.1.0 generation and create migrations. Keep module
and example migrations in sync. Do not hand-edit migration metadata.

## Verification

Run `dart run tool/check.dart`. It includes unit tests, actual PostgreSQL and
Serverpod network tests, and interoperability with the official JavaScript
client. It does not make paid API calls.

Live tests require explicit authorization, an environment-only key, and a
persisted cumulative budget. Do not reset the ledger or increase its limit to
make a failing test pass. Do not store a live key in examples, logs, or fixtures.

Read `docs/updating.md` before changing upstream pins or claiming new coverage.
Keep `docs/validation.md` honest about fixture, live, and untested behavior.

## Product acceptance and developer reviews

Read `ROADMAP.md` before narrowing the scope or claiming completion. Native Dart
DX is the main contract; TanStack compatibility can be an optional integration.
Use an independent consumer-development subagent on each implementation round.
It must write/run realistic cases and score the experience honestly out of ten.
Use GPT-6.1 Terra with low/medium reasoning for subagents. Never convert a green
test count or forwarded provider parameters into a full-support claim.
